Full-year guidance was reiterated ($84.5-86M revenue, AI customer revenue up 8-10%) while Q2 guidance implies a GAAP loss of $0.02 to income of $0.01 and adjusted EBITDA margin of 0-2%, as sales and marketing steps up and legacy runoff accelerates. Total SaaS ARR fell 4% to $73.4M, total RPO fell 18% to $71M, and AI-customer net retention held at 104% versus 117% a year ago.

Paylocity reported Q1 FY2027 total revenue of $451.7 million, up 11% YoY, with recurring and other revenue of $424.5 million up 12%, coming in $7.2 million above the top end of revenue guidance. Adjusted EBITDA was $159.5 million at a 35.3% margin, $3.5 million above the high end of guidance. Management raised FY2027 total revenue guidance by $30 million at the midpoint to $1.910-$1.925 billion and increased adjusted EBITDA guidance to $711.5-$721.5 million, passing through more than the Q1 beat; the raise reflects stable demand, strong retention, and the September 25 bp rate hike. GAAP gross margin was pressured year-over-year on staffing timing ahead of year-end, which management characterized as timing rather than structural.

Prospect Capital reported September-quarter net investment income of $76 million, or $0.15 per common share, with NAV of approximately $2.9 billion, or $5.36 per share, and a net debt to total assets ratio of 25%. The board approved a $200 million common share repurchase authorization and monthly distributions of $0.035 per share for November, December, and January. Originations were $90 million against $257 million of repayments and exits, producing net repayments of $167 million, while non-accruals fell to 0.2% at fair value and 1.8% at cost. No guidance was provided and the Q&A session drew no questions.

Organic net sales rose 0.6% excluding EABL (1.4% including), with volume -0.1% and price/mix +0.7%; reported net sales were up 1.2% to $4.9 billion. North America organic sales fell 3.6% (U.S. -3.7%) on weakness in Don Julio, Casamigos and Crown Royal, partly offset by Johnnie Walker and double-digit Guinness and Smirnoff Ice. Asia-Pac grew 4.1%, LAC 4.8%, India 3.4% and EMEA 2.4%. FY2027 guidance was reiterated unchanged: broadly flat organic net sales, low-to-mid-single-digit organic operating profit growth, and free cash flow of around $2 billion.

Peloton reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $559 million, up 2% YoY and $4 million above the midpoint of guidance, its third consecutive quarter of YoY revenue growth. Gross margin was 61.3% (up 975 bps YoY) and adjusted EBITDA was $168 million, both well above guidance, though roughly $25 million of the beat came from tariff favorability and lower recall costs; ex-those items adjusted EBITDA was $143 million, $3 million above the midpoint. Ending paid connected fitness subscriptions of 2.475 million hit the high end of guidance with 1.7% net churn. Full-year FY2027 revenue guidance of $2.3-2.4 billion (down ~4% at midpoint), ~54% gross margin, $475-525 million adjusted EBITDA and at least $350 million free cash flow were all unchanged from last quarter.

MACOM reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $424.8 million, up 62.7% year-over-year and 24.1% sequentially, with adjusted EPS of $2.09 versus $1.40 in Q3 and adjusted operating margin of 38.2%. Data center revenue reached a record $188.1 million (up ~37% sequentially), I&D $164.6 million (+23%) and telecom $72.1 million (+1%); Q4 book-to-bill was 1.4:1 and the company ended the year with record backlog on a full-year book-to-bill of 1.5:1. Q1 FY2027 guidance is $450-460 million in revenue, 62-63% adjusted gross margin and $2.21-2.29 adjusted EPS, with data center expected up ~15% sequentially and telecom flat to slightly down. Management said data center growth should exceed FY2026's 74% (base case ~80%) and I&D growth could top 30%, and flagged operating margin above 40% during FY2027.

Q1 FY2027 core revenue was $316.4M, up 14% YoY, with a non-GAAP operating margin of 39% (up 900 bps sequentially) and non-GAAP net income of $119.1M, up 70% YoY. Management called the quarter a beat, with TPV exceeding expectations by ~250 bps, AP/AR take rate of 16.2 bps, core ARPU up 4.1% YoY, and GAAP net income of $60M. FY2027 guidance reiterates core revenue of $1.28B-$1.31B (11%-14% growth) and ~33% non-GAAP operating margin, while GAAP profit guidance was raised to more than $180M and non-GAAP EPS guidance implies ~47% YoY growth. Management flagged Q2 as a growth trough (core revenue growth of 10%-13%) tied to a tough prior-year compare and continued restructuring adjustments, with improvement expected in the back half.

Hyperliquid Strategies reported Q1 FY2027 results dominated by treasury movements: net income of ~$621 million after a ~$172 million tax provision, driven by ~$803 million of unrealized HYPE gains as the token rose from $65.04 to $90.99. NAV rose ~82% to $3.4 billion, cash increased to ~$255 million with zero debt, and the company raised ~$911 million net, deploying $785 million into 9.1 million HYPE at an average $86.44 and $17 million into buybacks at $6.36. The company announced it is applying to form its own FCM as a neutral bridge for U.S. Hyperliquid customers, with a timeline of roughly three to six months and single-digit-million-dollar one-time cost; no formal financial guidance was provided and results are non-operating, driven by token price.

ScanSource reported Q1 FY2027 net sales growth of 30% year-over-year with reported net profits up 9%; non-GAAP net income was $17.7 million and non-GAAP EPS $0.86. Profitability was pressured by a lower-margin large-hardware mix (~110-120 bps of margin compression) and customer-specific bad debt reserves in Brazil tied to Oi S.A., which management characterized as largely confined to Q1. FY2027 guidance was raised to $3.8-4.0 billion net sales and $175-185 million adjusted EBITDA, now including the September 1 MicroAge acquisition, with free cash flow reaffirmed at least $85 million. Free cash flow was a $44 million use in Q1 on higher working capital, and share repurchases totaled $5 million with ~$116 million remaining on the authorization.

Revenue came in at $177.8 million, up 4.3% sequentially but down 2.6% year-over-year, slightly above the midpoint of guidance, with non-GAAP gross margin up 150 bps to 25.2% and a non-GAAP loss of $0.07 per share versus $0.13 loss last quarter. Advanced Computing grew over 50% sequentially and 80% year-over-year to nearly 23% of revenue, while traditional PC revenue fell roughly 30% sequentially and consumer was down 22.9% sequentially. December guidance is approximately $180 million plus or minus $10 million with non-GAAP gross margin of 25.7% plus or minus 1%, implying slight sequential and roughly 10% year-over-year growth despite continued PC weakness. Management flagged elevated memory costs and component shortages as a persistent headwind and said it does not expect a near-term PC recovery.

Q1 FY2027 GMV grew 34% and the RLTC take rate came in at 4.3%, with funding costs at 6% of on-balance-sheet loans. Management set a full-year FY2027 growth floor of at least 30% (a 'three handle'), noting Q2's first month is growing at a high-30s rate, and flagged a new transformer-based underwriting model that improved approval separation roughly twofold. Provision expense rose on September-dated approval experiments kept on balance sheet and GAAP operating margin guidance landed below Street on heavier warrant expense tied to new-user growth in the U.K. launch; DTC and wallets drove about half of volume.

BrasilAgro reported Q1 FY2027 net income of BRL 81 million and Adjusted EBITDA of BRL 95 million, driven by a BRL 50 million gain from farm sales and BRL 37 million in financial effects from soy price rallies. Management highlighted that operational results fell short of the BRL 150 million target due to lower corn sales volume compared to the prior year and tight sugarcane margins caused by low ATR prices. The company reduced its net debt/EBITDA ratio to 1.05x following the farm sale but noted that high interest rates are currently hindering further expansion or purchases.

Atlassian reported Q1 FY2027 total revenue of $1.8B, up 24% YoY, with cloud revenue up 31% to $1.3B and subscription ARR up 22.5% to $6.8B; GAAP operating margin was 11% and free cash flow was $463M (26% margin, up 304% YoY). RPO grew 44% to $4.7B and gross margin rose to 85.2%, but management flagged that Q2 cloud guidance implies about 4 points of deceleration and that ARR growth will decline over the next three quarters on tougher comps and lapping the DX acquisition. The full-year guide was raised by less than the size of the beat, which management attributed to a prudent stance amid macro and geopolitical uncertainty, and no meaningful usage-based pricing revenue is assumed in FY2027. Cloud revenue was modestly reduced by hybrid Data Center deals that shifted some revenue to Data Center.

Tapestry reported Q1 FY2027 revenue up 12% pro forma to $1.9 billion, operating margin up 230 bps to over 23%, and EPS up 32% to $1.82, beating guidance by about $0.27. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $8.5-8.6 billion (6-7% constant-currency growth), operating margin above 24%, and EPS to $8.25-$8.35 from a prior $7.80-$7.90, with increased shareholder returns of about $2 billion including $1.7 billion in buybacks. Coach grew 16% constant currency with broad regional strength (North America +7%, Greater China +41%, Europe +27%), while Kate Spade declined 10%, in line with guidance, with gross margin up 190 bps. Gross margin expanded 220 bps to 78.7%, including a 70-bp tariff benefit, and Q2 revenue is guided up 5-6% constant currency with EPS of about $3.05.

AMSC reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $94.0 million versus $65.9 million a year ago, up more than 40%, with Grid up 41% and Wind up 51%. Non-GAAP net income was $9.1 million, or $0.20 per share, flat with the year-ago $0.20, while GAAP net income fell to $3.0 million, or $0.06 per share, from $4.8 million, or $0.11, and gross margin compressed to 28% from 31% though it rose 190 bps sequentially. Q3 guidance calls for revenue above $80 million, net income above break-even, and non-GAAP net income above $7 million, or $0.15 per share, with management citing customer pull-ins that shifted projects into Q2 and a large semiconductor project that builds in Q3 but ships in Q4. Orders exceeded $95 million in Q2, first-half orders of about $230 million more than doubled year over year, and 12-month backlog of nearly $320 million rose 50% year over year.

H1 FY2027 operating income was JPY 2.2 trillion on sales of JPY 26.96 trillion, with net income of JPY 2.24 trillion; OI rose year-on-year as cost reduction, price revisions, value-chain profits and tariff mitigation offset Middle East disruption and material costs. Toyota revised full-year operating income guidance up JPY 500 billion to JPY 3.9 trillion, with revenue forecast at JPY 53.5 trillion on FX assumptions of JPY 157/USD and EUR 182. Consolidated vehicle sales fell 25,000 units YoY (but rose 26,000 ex-Hino), while Toyota/Lexus unit sales fell to 96% of the prior year on weak China demand and the Middle East, and the electrified ratio reached 55.6%. Shareholder returns were expanded: interim dividend of JPY 50 (up JPY 5), FY dividend of JPY 100, buyback authorization raised JPY 300 billion to JPY 1.3 trillion, and an additional 1 billion treasury shares cancelled.

Rockwell reported Q4 FY2026 core organic sales growth of 7% (reported +1%), adjusted EPS of $3.88 up 16%, and enterprise operating margin of 24.5% up 320 bps, though the margin included 130 bps of tariff-refund benefit and reported sales were cut ~$85 million by customer refunds. Intelligent Devices organic sales rose 5%, Software & Control +15% with Logix up 25%, and Lifecycle Services +2%; full-year core sales grew 9%, adjusted EPS $13.42 up 27%, and free cash flow conversion was 113%. FY2027 guidance calls for 6%-9% organic growth (7.5% midpoint), ~23% enterprise margin (up ~100 bps), and adjusted EPS of $14.50-$15.50 ($15.00 midpoint), with ARR growth expected to improve to 7% from 5%. Key soft spot was ARR, which management acknowledged 'did not meet our expectations' primarily due to project delays and scaled-back rollout scopes in Lifecycle Services.

NFG reported Q4 adjusted EPS of $1.22 (GAAP $1.02), flat versus the prior year, capping FY2026 adjusted EPS of $7.55, up 9% YoY; full-year Seneca production of 419.5 Bcf came in just below the low end of the already-revised guidance range. Initial FY2027 guidance is $6.00-$6.40 per share, well below FY2026, driven by a $2.85/MMBtu natural gas price assumption ($0.80 lower NYMEX) and flat production of 400-435 Bcf. Offsets include newly in-service Tioga Pathway and Shippingport Lateral projects (~$30 million incremental annual revenue), the closed Ohio utility acquisition doubling utility rate base, and anticipated operating income doubling in the utility segment. Management flagged 2027 as a transitional year with one-time separation costs and modest dilution from acquisition financing.

Doximity reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $174.5 million, up 4% year-over-year and 2% above the high end of guidance, with adjusted EBITDA of $89 million (51% margin) 9% above the high end. FY2027 revenue guidance was raised to $678-683 million (6% growth at midpoint, a $4.5 million midpoint increase), while adjusted EBITDA guidance of $317-325 million implies continued AI investment and a 47% midpoint margin. Non-GAAP gross margin fell to 88% from 92% last quarter on AI cost scaling, NRR slipped to 103% overall and 106% for top-20 customers, and Q3 revenue is guided to $195-196 million (6% growth).

Q4 net sales fell 1.1% to $376.5 million (Water Flow -3.0%, Water Management +1.4%), adjusted EPS was flat at $0.38, and adjusted EBITDA rose 4.0% to $95.5 million with margin up 130 bps to 25.4%. Full-year net sales grew 3.2% to ~$1.5 billion, adjusted EBITDA rose 14.1% to a record $372.2 million (25.2% margin, +240 bps), and adjusted EPS rose ~20% to $1.57 with $207.3 million of free cash flow. FY2027 guidance is net sales of $1.44-$1.47 billion (flat to +2.5% ex-metering) and adjusted EBITDA of $378-$388 million, a ~26.3% margin at the midpoint, down from $372.2 million on an absolute basis only slightly higher and reflecting the metering exit. The company also announced the transition of its metering business to ZENNER USA, with ~$40 million of metering sales at a negative EBITDA margin, ~$26 million of one-time FY2027 expenses, and a 100-140 bps annualized margin benefit. Additionally, the board authorized a $300 million buyback increase and a 14.3% dividend raise to $0.08 per quarter.

Total revenue of $601 million rose 6% YoY and beat the $585 million outlook; adjusted EBITDA of $234 million topped the $232 million guide at a 38.8% margin, and adjusted diluted EPS was $0.29 versus $0.25 prior year. FY2026 revenue guidance was raised to $2.34 billion and net CAPEX to $400 million, but adjusted EBITDA guidance was held at $920 million as higher Q4 activations, transfers and D&I mix dilute flow-through. Modular units on rent inflected up 1.2% YoY, the first growth in five years, and the modular order book is up over 20% YoY, supporting initial 2027 views of low single-digit organic revenue and mid-single-digit organic EBITDA growth.

Manulife reported record core EPS of $1.4 billion (up 6% YoY) and adjusted book value per share growth of 9%, driven by strong Asia results and a net favorable actuarial basis change. However, Global WAM pre-tax earnings were broadly in-line with the prior year due to $3.6 billion in net outflows from retirement business and lower ALDA returns. Management maintained its 18%+ ROE target for 2027 despite short-term headwinds.

Q3 revenue was $244.7M, up 10.4% and within guidance, with retail +12.4% and e-commerce +4.8%; adjusted gross margin 54.6% (+40 bps) and adjusted EBITDA $28.6M at 11.7% of revenue (+10 bps). Full-year revenue guidance was narrowed to $966-976M (11%-12% growth) and now includes up to 1 point of Intelligent Eyewear contribution, with adjusted EBITDA of $117-119M; Q4 revenue guided to $243-253M (15%-20% growth) on a much larger marketing and launch spend. Active customers grew only 3% and management flagged softer September trends, weak category units, and pressure on cash-pay consumers, offset by eye exams +30%, insurance +22%, and the Nov 12 Intelligent Eyewear pre-order launch. Guidance was nudged with a new product contribution rather than raised on the core business.

RenovoRx reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.07 million, up ~17% sequentially and more than fourfold from $266,000 a year ago, with gross margin of 82% (85% excluding zero-margin device conversions) and a net loss of $3.6 million, or $0.08 per share. Active commercial cancer centers rose to 26 from 21 at Q2, leaving a commercial funnel of more than 65 centers against a year-end 2026 target of 36. Management maintained (did not raise) full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $3.75-$4.25 million, and operating loss narrowed to $3.2 million from $3.4 million in the prior quarter. Cash of $10.4 million is expected to fund operations into the second half of 2027, and the phase III TIGeR-PaC trial has completed enrollment with top-line data expected in the second half of 2027.

Runway reported Q3 FY2026 total investment income of $40.6 million (up from $37 million in Q2) but net investment income fell to $15.9 million from $18.2 million, with NII per share of $0.38 including roughly $0.06 of net one-time benefit ($0.08 prepayment fees partly offset by $0.02 debt costs), implying a core run rate near $0.32 versus the $0.33 base dividend. NAV per share was $11.94 versus $11.91, and the portfolio shrank to $1.1 billion from $1.2 billion on $140 million of liquidity events (including the $72.3 million 3PL/Extensiv repayment) against only $8.5 million of deployments. Management guided that Q4 prepayments could match or exceed Q3, that net portfolio growth may take a while, and declined to commit to 2027 dividend coverage beyond stating they expect to cover the base dividend next quarter and full year; the board expanded the buyback to $30 million through September 2027.

Rayonier reported Q3 GAAP EPS of $0.41 on net income of $123 million, including $91 million of income from the ~36,000-acre Washington disposition; excluding that and $7 million of merger costs, EPS was $0.13 and adjusted EBITDA was $145 million, up sharply YoY on PotlatchDeltic contributions. Southern Timber adjusted EBITDA rose 23% to $52 million on 56% higher harvest volumes with delivered sawlog prices down 5% and pulpwood down 15% YoY (both up low-single digits sequentially), while Northwest Timber EBITDA jumped to $32 million from $6 million on doubled volumes and 29% higher sawlog prices. Wood Products EBITDA of $27 million was the best since Q3 2022 at $528/MBF lumber realization, but management guided Q4 realizations lower with quarter-to-date prices ~6% below Q3 and the Random Lengths composite 12% lower. Real Estate Q4 EBITDA is guided to $60-70 million, implying full-year toward the upper end of the $180-200 million range, buybacks totaled $60 million in Q3 with a $300 million authorization increase, and more timberland dispositions are planned over 12-18 months.

Q3 revenue rose 3% YoY to $738 million, in line with expectations of flat to low single-digit growth, while normalized adjusted EBITDA grew 13% to $170 million, beating the $155 million guide by $15 million and expanding margin 200 bps to 23%. Air marketplace bookings fell 1% on a 300-400 bps Middle East conflict and fuel-price headwind, though total marketplace bookings were flat and management expects sequential improvement into Q4. Full-year pro forma EBITDA guidance was raised $10 million to approximately $610 million and FCF guidance improved, while revenue and bookings growth outlooks were reaffirmed. Reported free cash flow was negative $48 million, attributed to $15 million of refinancing fees and $40 million of accrued interest, absent which it would have been positive.

Clinical-stage biotech with no product revenue; Q3 FY2026 net loss widened to $22.3 million from net income of $45.4 million a year earlier, the prior-year figure inflated by a $58.1 million warrant fair-value gain versus $3.6 million other income this year. R&D rose to $18.1 million from $9 million and G&A to $7.8 million from $3.7 million, driven by SAFEGUARD trial costs and stock-based compensation. The company ended the quarter with $205 million in cash and projects funding through 2028, including $13.4 million of warrant exercise proceeds. Enrollment guidance is unchanged: SAFEGUARD adult and adolescent cohorts are fully enrolled, pediatric step-down was approved by the DMC in September, full enrollment is reaffirmed for Q4 with top-line data in 2H 2027; FDA granted Fast Track designation in October.

StandardAero reported Q3 revenue of $1.56 billion, up 4% year-over-year, adjusted EBITDA of $225 million up 15% with margins expanding 130 bps to 14.4%, and adjusted diluted EPS up 30% to $0.39. The company raised full-year 2026 guidance across the board: revenue to $6.525-6.645 billion (~9% growth vs prior 6%), adjusted EBITDA to $905-920 million (~13% vs prior 11%), and adjusted EPS to $1.57-1.62 (~26% vs prior 23%), while reiterating adjusted free cash flow guidance of $270-300 million. The quarter reflected margin expansion in engine services and continued profitability on LEAP and CFM56 DFW programs, partially offset by military component repair delays tied to Middle Eastern conflict outlays. Management also announced an increase in share repurchase authorization to $1.01 billion and a $350 million accelerated share repurchase.

SandRidge reported Q3 FY2026 production of 20.9 MBOE/d, up 10% YoY with oil up 8%, revenue of $54 million (up 37% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $39 million (up 44% YoY). Adjusted net income was $23.8 million, or $0.64 per share, versus $15.5 million, or $0.42 per share, a year earlier; GAAP net income of $31 million ($0.83 per share) included a ~$14 million deferred tax revaluation benefit. The $48 million Cherokee bolt-on closed intra-quarter and added only partial-period production, with management citing roughly a 10% incremental production uplift and about 5% to annual volumes. No explicit updated production or capital guidance was issued beyond reaffirming the 10-well program and $10-12 million adjusted G&A, while management flagged emerging service-cost inflation in rig rates, tubulars and pressure pumping.

SEG reported Q3 FY2026 total operating EBITDA positive for a second straight quarter at $362K, a $3.2M/113% swing from the $2.9M loss in Q3 2025, with hospitality and entertainment positive and landlord operations at a loss. Management said the quarter underperformed expectations due to record Las Vegas heat (110F July, 105F August game highs) and a NYC nor'easter that forced cancellation of two sold-out Pier 17 concerts; concert series revenue fell 18% and Las Vegas revenue fell 4%. Offsets included G&A down 65% to $6.2M (down 4% excluding prior-year leadership costs), adjusted EPS loss narrowing 60% to $0.23, a net cash position of $72.2M, and net proceeds of ~$7.2M from the 85 South Street sale. No formal revenue or EBITDA guidance was given; capital spending to stabilization is tracking toward the high end of the $35-55M range, and Flanker Kitchen + Sports Bar and Hidden Boot Saloon openings slipped to late Q1/early Q2 2027 on contractor delays.

Solaris reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $341M (up 55% sequentially) and record adjusted EBITDA of $136M (up 26% sequentially), with Power Solutions revenue of $284M up 79% sequentially and Logistics revenue of $57M. Adjusted pro forma net income was $43M, or $0.45 per diluted share. Management raised Q4 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $165M-$185M from $145M-$180M and Q1 2027 guidance to $220M-$260M from $200M-$240M, and signed a 15-year, 900 MW contract that lifts weighted average contract tenor to ~11 years. Contracted backlog exceeds $16B of revenue (>$1.6B annual run-rate adjusted EBITDA once deployed), though total expected capital through 2029 rose ~$600M and management acknowledged share-price pressure tied to data-center policy concerns, mostly in Texas where it has minimal exposure.

Serve reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $2.8 million, up over 300% year-over-year and ahead of expectations, and raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $12 million from a prior $9-10 million (implying ~$3 million in Q4 and ~4.5x prior-year revenue). Gross loss was $7.6 million at a negative 266% gross margin, but this marked a third consecutive quarter of improvement, with fleet margin up over 100 percentage points sequentially and cost of revenues down 14%. GAAP net loss was $59.2 million (-$0.68/share), non-GAAP net loss $44.6 million (-$0.51/share), with non-GAAP opex down $1.2 million sequentially to $39.2 million and $198 million in cash and marketable securities. Management also launched Serve Physical AI Services and flagged a $20 million reduction in full-year non-GAAP opex expectations versus the start of the year.

Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 2% to $176.0 million, but comparable sales fell 6.4% on a 4.9% traffic decline and 2.1% mix headwind, with restaurant-level margin contracting 270 bps to 10.4% and adjusted EBITDA a $6.8 million loss versus a $4.4 million loss a year ago. Management guided Q4 comps to about +4% (including a 150 bp gift card lap headwind) and Q4 restaurant margin to roughly 11%, with one-time costs of about 60 bps, and set the full-year outlook at comps down about 5.5%, restaurant margin of 11-11.5%, and adjusted EBITDA of -$23 million to -$20 million. October comps turned positive at about +5% with 4% transaction growth, and management sized roughly 150 bps of food-cost and a couple hundred bps of labor-efficiency opportunity for 2027 while cutting 2027 net new openings to about half the 2026 level.

Shake Shack reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $423.3M, up 15.2% YoY, with company-operated same-Shack sales growth of 2.5% (0.8% traffic, 1.7% price mix), and adjusted EBITDA of $62.8M, up 16%. Restaurant-level margin was 22.5%, down 30 bps YoY, as food and paper leverage (down 100 bps to 28.3% of sales) was offset by higher labor (25.4%, +50 bps) and other operating expenses (+90 bps) tied to delivery commissions. Guidance was maintained but skewed to the low end: full-year adjusted EBITDA toward the low end of $225M-$235M, G&A toward the low end of the 12%-13% range, and 60-65 company-operated openings; licensed openings now expected at the high end of 40-45. Management flagged a Q4 lap of last year's 1-3-5 value platform and Big Shack launch, plus ~20-50 bps of traffic headwind from new-Shack delivery transfer.

Steven Madden reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $772.6M, up 15.7% YoY, with diluted EPS of $0.79 versus $0.43, up 85%. Gross margin expanded to 44.6% from 43.4% and operating income rose to $78.9M (10.2% of revenue) from $46.3M. Management raised FY2026 guidance to revenue growth of 12-13% (from 11-13%) and EPS of $2.15-$2.20 (from $2.05-$2.15). Kurt Geiger's full-year outlook was trimmed to low double digits from mid-teens as comps normalized to 6%, and Q4 wholesale is guided down 6-7% on shipment timing shifts.

Q3 FY2026 net revenue was $16.2 million, up 38% YoY, with implant unit volume up 34% and gross margin expanding to 78.5% from 76.2%. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $68-70 million (44-48% growth) from a prior $67-69 million (42-46%). Net loss narrowed to $7.0 million from $8.7 million, and Adjusted EBITDA loss improved to $5.5 million, with cash of $92.3 million. Q4 is guided for similar gross margins but higher SG&A as a percentage of revenue and moderately increased cash burn.

SINTX reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $2.2 million, up 953% year-over-year from $208,000, and roughly double the high end of its prior $900,000-$1.1 million guidance, driven by aerospace and industrial technical manufacturing. Gross margin expanded to 62% from 45%, gross profit rose to about $1.4 million from $93,000, opex fell 13% to $3 million, and net loss narrowed 55% to $1.6 million. However, management withdrew visibility on Q4, stating it cannot offer an expectation on delivery of the remaining portion of the $3.2 million in June purchase orders relative to Q4 2026. Cash fell to $2 million from $4.1 million at year-end 2025, with $6.6 million used in operations year-to-date and continued operating losses flagged.

Q3 revenue of $69.2M came in at the upper end of the $65-70M guide but still declined 2.1% YoY, a sharp moderation from -7.8% in Q2. Adjusted gross margin rose ~380 bps to 71.8% (helped by a one-time ~$1M / ~140 bps tariff refund), adjusted EBITDA was $13.4M (19.3% margin, up ~50%), and GAAP operating income of ~$5M marked a second straight positive quarter; consumables returned to growth (+1.2%), equipment fell 9.9%. FY26 revenue guidance was trimmed at the bottom to $281-287M from $280-290M while adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $48-50M from $39-46M. The company also repaid its remaining $103.2M 2026 converts, ending with $112.4M cash; Q4 gross margin is expected to moderate as the tariff benefit laps and opex steps up.

Core FFO was $0.64/share vs $0.60 a year ago (+6.7%), driven by 4.2% same-center NOI growth and accretive acquisitions; other revenues rose 11%. Full-year 2026 core FFO guidance was raised to $2.49-$2.53 from $2.45-$2.52 (+8% at midpoint), and the low end of same-center NOI growth was lifted to 3.5% from 2.75% with the high end unchanged at 4.25%. Occupancy reached 97.3% (+70 bps from June), blended cash rent spreads were 11% on ~560 leases signed over 12 months, and TTM tenant sales were $487/sq ft (+2.5%), with the occupancy cost ratio steady at 9.7%. The board authorized a $0.3125 quarterly dividend, a 7% increase year over year.

NuScale reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $0.3 million versus $8.2 million a year earlier, with management attributing the drop to the absence of RoPower FEED Phase II work in the current quarter. Operating expenses fell to $65 million from $549 million in the prior-year period, and liquidity rose to roughly $1.9 billion from about $916 million. No revenue or margin guidance was issued; management said OpEx should stay fairly constant until an ENTRA1/TVA project ramps, and that margin clarity requires an OEM agreement. The key business development was a first-article manufacturing agreement with Doosan Enerbility, though TVA and RoPower commercial agreements remain unfinalized.

Same-store weighted occupancy reached 88.6% (+200 bps YoY), same-store RevPOR rose 4.6% to $5,413 and resident revenue grew 7.3% to $163.5 million, lifting same-store NOI 15.6% with 230 bps of margin expansion to 31.8%. Normalized FFO was $0.46 per share and Adjusted EBITDA rose 26.2% to $46.8 million, while total SHOP NOI margin of 29.1% was up 240 bps YoY but down 80 bps sequentially on Q3 seasonality. Net leverage rose to 8.1x from 7.8x at June 30, and formal 2027 guidance is deferred to the Q4 call, with management only indicating occupancy and rate growth should be consistent with recent years.

South Bow reported Q3 FY2026 normalized EBITDA of $248 million and DCF of $187 million (up 7% QoQ, aided by a one-time favorable tax adjustment), with management describing results as in line with expectations. Full-year 2026 DCF guidance was raised 4% to ~$690 million while 2026 normalized EBITDA guidance stayed unchanged at ~$1.04 billion. 2027 guidance was introduced: normalized EBITDA of ~$1.07 billion (±2%) and DCF of ~$630 million (±4%), the DCF decline reflecting higher current income taxes versus tax savings in 2026; a $0.50 quarterly dividend was declared and $320 million of notes were repurchased. Leverage stood at 4.3x with net debt ~$4.4 billion, and Prairie Connector remains targeted for mid-2027 FID pending permit durability.

Solventum reported Q3 FY2026 sales of $1.95 billion, down 7% reported and 2.8% organic, as the reversal of $125 million in ERP-related advanced orders from Q2 created a ~630 bps organic headwind; normalized organic growth was ~4%. EPS was $1.45 including a ~$0.35 hit from the order reversal, gross margin rose 120 bps YoY to 57.1%, and operating margin fell 70 bps to 19.9% (~22.3% excluding the ERP timing). Management nudged FY2026 organic growth to the high end of the 2.5%-3% range, moved operating margin toward the high end of 22.2%-22.7%, and raised EPS guidance to $7.20-$7.30 from $7.10-$7.20 while maintaining $200-300M free cash flow. The renegotiated 3M supply agreement eliminated an anticipated 100 bps 2027 gross margin headwind, and separation is now more than 90% complete.

SoundHound reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $62.4 million, up 48% year-over-year, including nearly one month (~26 days, ~$14 million) of LivePerson contribution following the September 4 close. Non-GAAP gross margin was 50.3%, down 9 percentage points year-over-year on new agentic AI ramp and higher cloud usage. FY2026 revenue guidance was narrowed and the midpoint raised to $250-260 million from $230-260 million, while FY2027 revenue guidance of $350-400 million was reaffirmed alongside a first-time target of sustainable positive adjusted EBITDA in the second half of 2027, supported by at least $120 million of identified annualized cost reductions ($80 million actioned before January 1). The key change is a shift away from point-in-time license revenue (cut to ~10% of revenue from ~33% in Q2) toward hosted recurring structures, which management says drives the ~$35 million reduction versus an additive ~$290 million 2026 base.

SPG reported Q3 real estate FFO of $3.37/share, up 4.7% YoY, with domestic property NOI +6.6% and portfolio NOI +6.7%. Comparable mall and outlet sales rose 4.9% and occupancy reached 96.5%, the highest combined level since 2016, while initial new-deal rents jumped 17% YoY with tenant allowances down 10%. Management raised full-year 2026 real estate FFO guidance by $0.10 to $13.30-$13.40/share (about 5% growth at the midpoint) and declared a $2.30 Q4 dividend, up 4.5% YoY. Reported FFO of $3.09 was reduced by $0.27/share of non-cash mark-to-market and equity revaluation losses, and management flagged roughly $0.30 of interest expense headwind for 2027.

Total company revenue was $274.3 million with adjusted operating income of $39.2 million; the Sphere segment grew revenue 14% YoY to $198.9 million and segment AOI rose to $32.4 million from $17.1 million on 241 Wizard of Oz performances versus 220 combined prior-year showings. MSG Networks deteriorated sharply, with revenue down to $75.4 million from $88.4 million and AOI to $6.8 million from $19.3 million on a ~15.5% subscriber decline, prompting a non-cash goodwill impairment charge. No quantitative guidance was given, but management said it still expects growth in 2027, reaffirmed 3-4 Sphere Experiences by end-2027, and guided to a new venue announcement likely this quarter. The main negative changes were the MSG Networks impairment and the scrapping of the From the Edge concept.

Total revenue was $37.7 million versus $32.5 million in Q3 2025, including $33.4 million in U.S. neffy net product revenue, $2.6 million in ex-U.S. supply revenue, and $1.7 million in collaboration revenue. Total U.S. market share surpassed 5% (from 4% a year ago), end-user demand rose 42% year-over-year, and field-targeted account share improved to 9% from 6%. SG&A fell to $43.5 million, down more than 40% from the first-half 2026 quarterly average, and the company reaffirmed its path to cash flow breakeven by year-end 2027 on $138.4 million in cash. Net revenue growth lagged demand growth due to inventory timing, and gross-to-net remains around 50%.

Sempra reported Q3 FY2026 GAAP EPS of $1.34 versus $0.12 a year ago and adjusted EPS of $1.40, up 26% from $1.11. Management guided to the high end of the 2026 adjusted EPS range of $4.80-$5.30, affirmed the 2027 range of $5.10-$5.70 and the 7%-9% long-term EPS growth rate, while flagging that pending regulatory outcomes could put 2027 results in the lower half of the range. Texas drove the quarter with $154 million of higher equity earnings, and Oncor plans a roughly 20% increase to its $47.5 billion capital plan in February 2027. A CPUC proposed decision denying the GRC petition for modification creates a $188 million revenue requirement headwind, limiting California earnings to the low end of its 2027 guidance range if not corrected.

Gibraltar reported Q3 FY2026 Residential net sales of $399M (up 73% on OmniMax inclusion, +3.1% organic) with adjusted EBITDA of $84M (up 62.3%) and adjusted EPS of $1.01, which included a $21.5M net interest impact. Each segment came in below management expectations: shingle shipments fell 13% YoY and 22% sequentially, Agtech pushed more than $40M of revenue out of H2 on permit delays, and Infrastructure sales fell 7.8% on fiber seal pilot delays. Full-year 2026 guidance for continuing operations was cut to sales of $1.64-1.66B, adjusted EPS of $2.25-2.40 (from $3.92 in 2025), and free cash flow of roughly 1% of sales, versus prior expectations of residential down ~5% in H2 now assumed down ~15%. OmniMax integration synergies were raised to a $36.5M annualized run rate, and the D.S. Brown/Infrastructure sale ($208M) was signed for expected Q4 close.

RLJ reported comparable RevPAR of $153, up 9.7% YoY, on ADR +6.4% to $203 and occupancy +230 bps to 75.4%, with each month beating expectations. Hotel EBITDA rose 17.5% to $93.9 million at a 26.5% margin (up 190 bps), adjusted EBITDA was $85 million (+17.3%), and adjusted FFO per share was $0.34 (+25.9%). Full-year comparable RevPAR guidance was raised to 5.75%-6.25% (up 200 bps at the midpoint), and corporate adjusted EBITDA guidance rose $9 million at the midpoint to $352-$358 million. The company also sold seven Chicago Midway hotels for $110 million at a 14x 2026 forecasted EBITDA multiple.

Stoneridge reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted revenue of $180 million, up 30% (nearly 26% core, excluding FX and $6 million Mexico contract manufacturing), the fastest organic growth in over three years, with adjusted EBITDA up over 40% YoY to $7.3 million (4.1% margin, +34 bps). However, adjusted gross margin fell 382 bps to 19.9% on inventory-related expenses and legacy warranty settlements ($3 million incremental), and reported results absorbed a ~$24 million non-cash pre-tax charge tied to a $25.5 million arbitration award on former Control Devices PM sensor claims. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $690-700 million ($37.5 million higher at midpoint), but adjusted EBITDA is now expected at the bottom of the $20-25 million range due to memory-chip inflation, unfavorable FX, and the legacy-matter costs. MirrorEye hit a record $37 million in sales (+48% YoY), and a new non-MirrorEye vision system win is expected to add ~$180 million through 2028, ramping from early 2027.

Q3 FY2026 total revenues were $33 million, down $244.8 million year-over-year, driven by a $128.6 million unrealized Babcock & Wilcox loss versus a $30.2 million prior-year gain, producing a net loss of $243 million and diluted LPS of $6.04; Adjusted EBITDA was negative $219.1 million while Operating Adjusted EBITDA was $2.9 million. Service and fee revenues fell $58.2 million to $112.5 million on lower ATM/private placement/underwriting fees and lower SpaceX carried interest, partly offset by $6.3 million higher M&A and advisory fees. The capital markets segment posted negative $90.2 million of revenue and a $120 million segment loss; communications income rose to $13.2 million and Targus lost $4.3 million. Management gave no formal guidance beyond calling Operating Adjusted EBITDA 'on plan' for the year, citing up to $50 million in expected SpaceX cash inflows to fund the $164 million December senior note redemption and the pending Sangoma acquisition, which is targeted to close in January 2027 and add $35-40 million of EBITDA.

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $9.8 million, up 86% YoY, split $5.7 million capital and $4.1 million recurring (disposables/service); gross margin rose to 78% from 74% on favorable mix and price discipline. Net loss improved 3% to $7.7 million ($0.21/share vs $0.26), and operating cash use fell to $5 million from $11.3 million sequentially and $9.6 million a year ago. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance improved to at least $25 million (from approximately $25 million) with gross margin of 70% or higher. Installed base reached 98 systems globally (~70/30 US/international), qualified pipeline was $79.2 million, and management disclosed new Cook Medical distribution and Telix education agreements plus a CEO transition effective January 14, 2027.

Privia raised its 2026 outlook above the high end of initial guidance across all key financial metrics: implemented providers ~6,000 (11.5% growth), practice collections +13.1% at the midpoint, care margin +16.3%, and adjusted EBITDA +23.9% to a midpoint above the prior high end. Year-to-date practice collections rose 12% to $2.91 billion and adjusted EBITDA grew 21.9% to $114.7 million, or 28.8% of care margin, with $446.3 million of cash and no debt. Management is exiting the Montana Surgery Partners partnership (~$23 million annual practice collections, 69 providers) effective January 2027 with no material EBITDA impact, and announced the ~$36 million cash acquisition of Cano Health's American Choice MSSP ACO (~36,000 attributed lives). Cash flow conversion guidance was trimmed to ~70% of EBITDA from the prior 70%-80%, citing MSSP payment timing and full cash taxpaying status.

Q3 FY2026 net sales were $202.1M, down 1% YoY but up 32.5% sequentially from $152.5M, with net income of $29.9M ($1.30/diluted share) versus $1.20 a year ago. Gross margin expanded to 29.7% from 23.9% YoY, though that included a $3.8M tariff refund worth ~188 bps, and operating income was a record $40.9M (20.2% margin); operating cash flow was $40.9M and net cash reached ~$34M. Management raised its second-half outlook to net sales above 2H 2025 (prior: roughly in line), but guided Q4 gross margin down from Q3 on the non-recurring tariff refund plus a modest mix-driven further decline, and said it is not predicting a specific data center revenue level. Oil and gas softness continued (Power Systems sales down $6.2M YoY), partly offset by data center demand, and a new $220M three-year revolver cut borrowing spread 80 bps to SOFR+180.

Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 7% to $194.1 million with same-restaurant sales up 1.4% (2.1% check, -0.7% transactions) and Adjusted EBITDA up 23.7% to $26.5 million, 13.6% margin. Restaurant-level Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 50 bps to 20.7%, with labor 60 bps favorable. Full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $98-$101 million, but the company will close a mid to high single-digit number of underperforming non-Chicago restaurants, mostly in Q4, with material charges. 2027 plan includes 4-6 openings and 2%-3% annual same-restaurant sales.

Palvella reported no product revenue for Q3 FY2026, with R&D rising to $10.8 million from $6.5 million and G&A to $11.9 million from $3.6 million year over year, producing a net loss of $24.6 million, or $1.70 per share. Cash and equivalents/short-term investments were $236.7 million at quarter end, down from roughly $250 million at Q2, and full-year 2026 cash expenses are expected below prior guidance with Q4 as the largest investment period. The key event was FDA acceptance of the QTORIN rapamycin NDA in microcystic lymphatic malformations with Priority Review and a PDUFA date of February 28, 2027, alongside plans to initiate Phase III studies in cutaneous venous malformations and Phase III in DSAP this quarter. Management declined to provide 2027 revenue guidance, pointing to a launch phase in which revenue and demand are expected to be decoupled during payer and access ramp.

Q3 global system-wide sales fell 5.6% in constant currency to $1.15 billion, revenue dropped 10.5% to $455 million, and adjusted EBITDA fell $10 million to $38 million. North America comps and international comps (down 1.8%) both declined, with management citing an intensely promotional environment and soft new-customer acquisition; full-year guidance was cut to roughly -5% system sales, ~-8% North America comps, and approximately $175 million adjusted EBITDA, and Q4 is implied similar to Q3. CEO Penegor conceded top line came in below expectations and introduced the 'Unbox Better' strategy alongside a franchisee marketing framework approved by 98% of votes, a supply-chain margin reduction to 4%, and a tech-fee cut to 1.5%. Free cash flow was $19 million YTD versus $59 million last year; guidance assumes no improvement in the consumer environment and no benefit from Unbox Better.

Adjusted operating revenues rose 8% to $902 million and diluted adjusted operating EPS rose 7% to $6.77, but adjusted net operating income grew only 2% to $209 million on a smaller remeasurement gain ($9 million vs $23 million prior year). The investments business set records, with total ISP sales up 19%, variable annuities up 29%, managed accounts up 27%, AUM up 10% to $140 billion, and $407 million of net client flows. Term life was the weak spot: issued policies fell 7%, premiums fell 5%, and recruiting declined 10% year-over-year, with management guiding full-year 2026 issued policies down 8%-10% and year-end sales force down about 3%. Q4 guidance points to term life issued policies down low-single-digits and ISP sales up mid-single-digits.

Q3 revenue was $9.1 million, up 233% year over year, with non-GAAP gross margin of 74.6%. Bookings were $98 million in the quarter and roughly $104 million year to date, with full-year bookings expected above $120 million. Management raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $31-$34 million from $28-$32 million and reiterated greater than 100% revenue growth for 2027 off the higher base. Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $80.5 million from $45.3 million as R&D rose to $97.5 million, and the company ended with over $1.9 billion in cash and no debt.

Q3 FY2026 revenue fell to $212,000 from $552,000 a year ago, with nine-month revenue of $814,000 versus $2 million; gross margin was 35% for the quarter and 39% year-to-date. Full-year revenue guidance was reiterated at approximately $1 million, while adjusted OpEx guidance was lowered to $87 million or less from $98 million and total cash usage to $87 million or less from $93 million. Adjusted operating expenses were $18.2 million versus $21.4 million a year ago and declined sequentially, with roughly $12 million in annualized savings from the August restructuring; net loss narrowed to $22.3 million from $35.7 million. Proteus remains on track for a Q2 2027 launch, but AI-driven demand is lengthening lead times on certain components, prompting earlier orders and incremental working capital, with cash of $149.4 million funding operations into Q4 2028.

AVITA Medical reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $26.1 million, up 53% year-over-year and 20% sequentially, led by U.S. RECELL revenue of $22.4 million (up ~20% QoQ) on 3,196 units. Gross margin expanded 270 bps to 84%, operating expenses held flat at $24.6 million, net loss narrowed to $6.2 million ($0.20/share), and net cash use fell to ~$600,000 from $3.2 million in Q2. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance for the second consecutive quarter to $92-$94 million from $86-$89 million and reaffirmed Q4 cash flow breakeven, while noting Q3 likely benefited by roughly $1 million from summer burn seasonality. The going concern doubt was alleviated and the remaining $10 million Perceptive tranche was drawn.

Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 1.9% to $215.9 million with net income of $44.4 million ($0.70 diluted) versus $39.9 million ($0.60), and adjusted operating income grew 8.4% to $66.1 million with adjusted EPS of $0.77, up 18.5%. Total enrollments increased 1.6%, with AIU System up 7.5% to 10,830 and St. Augustine revenue up 9.8% to $41.7 million, while CTU enrollments were roughly flat at 31,870. Full-year 2026 adjusted operating income guidance was set at $260-263 million versus $237.9 million in 2025, with Q4 adjusted EPS guided to $0.68-0.72 versus $0.59. The company declared a $0.17 quarterly dividend and repurchased 610,000 shares for $19.9 million, and announced a definitive agreement to acquire South University (~10,500 students) expected to close as early as April 2027.

Radian reported Q3 2026 revenue of $624 million, more than double year-over-year with Inigo included, adjusted pre-tax operating income of $254 million, and adjusted net operating income of $1.44 per diluted share, up 25% YoY, with operating ROE of 16% versus roughly 13% a year earlier. Mortgage insurance generated $206 million of adjusted pre-tax operating income at a 37% combined ratio on record $286 billion primary insurance in force, while specialty net premiums earned fell 3% YoY to $311 million but produced an 80% combined ratio aided by $43 million of favorable prior-period development and benign catastrophe activity. Full-year buybacks of $379 million, or 8% of beginning shares, far exceeded the prior $200-$250 million guide, and the Q4 dividend from Radian Guaranty of $145 million lifts the 2026 total to $660 million versus initial $600 million guidance. No explicit forward EPS or combined-ratio guidance was raised; management flagged a more competitive specialty market and reiterated a low-90s normalized specialty combined ratio.

Q3 revenue grew 5.4% YoY to $109 million but declined sequentially, with defense tech revenue down YoY (~16% per Q&A) on UAS shipment timing while space rose over 30% organically. Gross margin hit a record 32.3% (vs 16.3% a year ago), backlog rose 14.3% sequentially to a record $619.7 million on 1.73 book-to-bill, but the quarter still showed a $23.2 million net loss and negative $5.3 million Adjusted EBITDA. Management reaffirmed the full-year 2026 revenue range of $450-500 million, citing backlog and $46.8 million of WIP/finished goods inventory now up $10.6 million sequentially, and attributed near-term lumpiness to milestone and delivery timing.

First quarter as Real REMAX Group: revenue $728M up 28% YoY (pro forma combined ~$770M, +20%), Adjusted EBITDA $34M up 66%, but GAAP operating loss of $72M and net loss of $67.2M driven by $78.7M of non-recurring acquisition costs. Management introduced 2027 guidance of $2.6-2.8B revenue and $175-190M Adjusted EBITDA on assumptions of 5-10% lower existing home sales and 3-4% lower prices, and Q4 revenue of $575-625M with $32-38M EBITDA. Cost actions exceeded plan — $40M+ gross savings actioned and 2027 synergy target lifted above $30M versus the original $30M — but North American RE/MAX agent count fell 3% and management off-boarded over 1,000 agents, with Tamir calling 2027 'another very challenging year.'

PRA Group reported Q3 2026 revenues of $286 million, portfolio income up 5% to $271 million, net income of $15 million, and cash collections of $536 million, 1% above internal expectations. TTM adjusted EBITDA grew 9% to $1.4 billion, adjusted operating expenses fell 6%, and net leverage declined to 2.6x for an eighth straight quarter of deleveraging. Guidance was largely unchanged: portfolio purchases remain on track for $1 billion-$1.3 billion, 2026 cash growth is expected to moderate versus 2025, and legal collection costs are expected to peak and decline in 2027. The main change versus the prior period was a sharp moderation in curve-adjustment revenue to $14 million after Q2's $349 million European write-up, shifting more revenue toward recurring portfolio income.

Reforation reported Q3 FY2026 net revenue up 19.1% YoY to $173.6 million, its 22nd consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, with DTC up 16.7% to $152.8 million and wholesale up 40.8% to $20.8 million. Gross margin expanded 250 bps to 60.4% (200 bps excluding ~$800,000 of tariff refunds) and adjusted EBITDA rose 64.2% to $23.1 million at a 13.3% margin, though GAAP swung to a $1.1 million net loss ($0.02/share) on $10.5 million of IPO-related stock comp and a 165.9% effective tax rate. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $610-612 million (20-21% growth, above the mid-to-high teens algorithm) and put adjusted EBITDA margin at ~14.2%, the high end of the prior range. Q4 is framed as prudent given a back-half-weighted holiday and a dynamic macro backdrop.

Research Frontiers reported Q3 FY2026 fee income of roughly $77,000 versus roughly $359,000 a year earlier, with the prior-year period including non-recurring government contract royalty revenue, and a net loss of about $510,000 versus just under $300,000. Cash at September 30 was about $645,000 with roughly $538,000 in working capital. Management said it does not expect material royalty recovery until after Q4 2026, tied to Gauzy's court-approved Israeli settlement, October financing, and initial payments toward restarting emulsion production in Israel and film coating in Germany. The company also disclosed NASDAQ listing notices on bid price and market value of listed securities, with a board decision on a hearing request possible in December.

Riley Permian reported Q3 FY2026 oil production of 25.4 MBbl/d, up 20% QoQ and 38% YoY, with total production of 42 MBOE/d, up 23% sequentially, despite wells turned to sales coming in below the low end of guidance. Cash flow from operations was $111 million, up 75% QoQ, and debt was reduced by $28 million to $245 million. Management did not provide formal 2027 guidance but previewed 30%-40% YoY oil and total production growth with a two-rig program and added ~90 net San Andres locations at Red Lake, while Q4 CapEx is expected to rise and full-year CapEx guidance increases. The quarter showed strong production conversion, but the soft well count and higher CapEx, plus withheld formal guidance, temper the read.

Permian Resources reported Q3 FY2026 oil production of 208,000 bbl/d (up ~10,000 bbl/d QoQ, ~8,000 organic) and total production of 458,000 BOE/d, with record free cash flow of $0.98 per share. Controllable cash costs fell 6% QoQ to a company-low $7.05/BOE (LOE $5.11/BOE, cash G&A $0.73/BOE), and gas revenue swung from -$90 million in Q2 to over +$50 million. The company raised full-year oil guidance to a 202,000 bbl/d midpoint (7% above February guidance) and now expects ~$300 million (~$0.35/share) more free cash flow than its original plan, while announcing $1.15 billion of acquisitions including Ridge Runner. Q4 oil is guided to more than 210,000 bbl/d, and cash CapEx was updated to a $2.025 billion midpoint.

Pennant reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $302.3M, up 32% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of $24.7M (+42.4%), adjusted EBITDA prior to NCI of $26.1M (+44%), and adjusted EPS of $0.35 (+16.7%). Home Health and Hospice segment revenue rose 38.2% to $239.8M with adjusted EBITDA of $38.1M (+42%), while Senior Living revenue grew 12.6% to $62.4M but segment adjusted EBITDA was roughly flat YoY due to integration challenges and elevated benefits costs. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance but called out higher-than-anticipated employee benefits costs (about 50 bps of revenue in Q3 and expected similar in Q4) and softness in two senior living markets; the home health final rule provided a 2.1% net increase (1.5% on Pennant claims).

Royal Gold reported record revenue of $465 million (up 84% YoY) on record volume of 109,000 GEOs, with record adjusted net income of $238 million ($2.80/share) and record operating cash flow of $344 million (up 98% YoY). Adjusted EBITDA margin increased to 84%, and the company fully repaid its revolver to become debt-free after quarter end. Management raised full-year guidance for other metals and expects silver and copper at or above the top end of ranges, while gold sales remain on track around the midpoint; Kansanshi copper guidance was narrowed and Andacollo guided to the low end. Portfolio developments include a Kinross buyback of 25% of the Great Bear royalty (~$43 million) in Q4, RIGI approval at MARA, and a temporary production suspension at Antamina following a fatality.

Regenxbio reported Q3 2026 cash, equivalents, and marketable securities of $251 million versus $241 million at year-end 2025, driven by a $100 million AbbVie NAAVIGATE milestone and $108 million in net proceeds from a July public offering; the total excludes a $39 million October Sarepta settlement payment. Royalty revenue came in slightly above one analyst's model on Itvisma pickup as U.S. Zolgensma IP has expired, though no explicit revenue or EPS figures were disclosed. Management guided to cash runway into late Q4 2027, spanning sura-vec wet AMD top-line data this quarter, a Q1 2027 RGX-202 BLA filing (switched from rolling to a single submission), and a 2027 sura-vec regulatory submission, with RGX-202 potential U.S. approval in H2 2027. No hard revenue, EPS, or margin results were reported, leaving the quarter defined by pipeline milestones rather than financial performance.

Playtika reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $673.8M, down 7.8% sequentially and essentially flat year-over-year, with record adjusted EBITDA of $252.1M (up 15.9% YoY, 37.4% margin) and net income of $40.4M. Guidance was reaffirmed, not raised: full-year revenue of $2.75B-$2.85B and adjusted EBITDA of $750M-$790M, now expected around the midpoint of both ranges versus last quarter's cautious second-half view. The quarter was driven by DTC revenue of $275.1M (40.8% of total, up 31.4% YoY), June's Journey up 12.1% and Slotomania stabilizing, offset by Bingo Blitz down 18.2% and Disney Solitaire down 21.9% sequentially. The board concluded its strategic review, opting to remain independent, with refinancing of upcoming maturities the stated priority.

Rigel reported Q3 FY2026 net product sales of $72.3 million, up 13% YoY, driven by $6.6 million from newly launched VEPPANU (six weeks of availability) on top of TAVALISSE $46 million (+3%), REZLIDHIA $9.9 million (+20%), and GAVRETO $9.8 million (-11%). Total revenues were $80.9 million with net income of $13.2 million, down from $27.9 million a year ago on higher costs and expenses of $63.8 million. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was narrowed to $290-$295 million from $285-$295 million, while the non-VEPPANU product sales range was trimmed to $255-$260 million from $255-$265 million and contract revenue raised to $35 million. Management struck an upbeat tone on the VEPPANU launch (100+ patients in six weeks, 88% PA approval) and reiterated R289 dose selection and registrational trial initiation plans for 2027.

Pulse Biosciences reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $395,000 versus $86,000 in the prior year period, with GAAP net loss widening to $23.1 million from $19.4 million and non-GAAP net loss to $17.5 million from $13.5 million. The company completed NANOPULSE-AF pivotal enrollment at 169 evaluable patients (189 total) in under six months, three months ahead of plan, and ended the quarter with $189.2 million in cash and marketable securities after raising $95.8 million through its ATM during the quarter. Management guided future quarterly non-GAAP costs and expenses to rise 15%-25% above the Q2/Q3 average of approximately $20 million, citing persistent AF IDE, additional studies, and manufacturing build-out; no revenue guidance was provided.

Surf Air reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $36.5 million, within its $35.5-$37.5 million guidance range and up 25% year-over-year and 24% quarter-over-quarter, with an Adjusted EBITDA loss of $6.7 million inside the $4-$7 million guide and 36% better than Q2. Surf On Demand revenue more than doubled to $19 million (+121% YoY) and surpassed scheduled service revenue of $17.5 million, which fell 15% YoY on EAS route exits, while airline Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $1.2 million. Full-year revenue guidance of $128-$138 million was reaffirmed, but the full-year Adjusted EBITDA loss outlook was widened to $32-$35 million from the prior range due to higher fuel prices (up ~37% per gallon YoY) and extended SurfOS implementation periods; SurfOS revenue was not material in the quarter. Q4 guidance was set at $36.4-$46.4 million revenue and a $2.4-$5.4 million Adjusted EBITDA loss, and no 2027 guidance or breakeven date was provided.

Starling Oncology reported record Q3 revenue of $169.8 million, up 24.3% year-over-year, with Adjusted EBITDA of $3.4 million (versus $0.2 million in Q2 and a $3.5 million loss a year ago) that exceeded the top end of the guided Q3 range. Specialty pharmacy revenue rose 44% to $109.3 million at a 24.2% gross margin, which management attributed partly to rebates and favorable drug price moves it does not expect to recur, guiding pharmacy margins to normalize to the high teens. Total gross margin expanded roughly 420 bps to 18.1%, and the MLR improved to 81% from 85.5% in Q2. However, the capitated revenue target for 2027 was cut to roughly $220 million from a prior $300 million after anchor Florida partners did not expand statewide, which analysts pressed on throughout; management reaffirmed 100% capitated revenue growth in 2027 versus 2026 and full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $4 million-$6 million.

Willdan reported Q3 FY2026 contract revenue of $215 million (+18% YoY) and net revenue of $112 million (+18%), with organic net revenue growth of 12% and 17% growth in the energy segment. Adjusted EBITDA rose 22% to $28.3 million, a 25.2% net revenue margin up 80 bps, while Adjusted EPS was essentially flat at $1.20 versus $1.21 on a higher tax rate and stock comp. Management raised FY2026 targets to net revenue of $435-445 million, Adjusted EBITDA of $109-111 million, and Adjusted EPS of $5.15-5.25, and introduced preliminary 2027 targets of $1 billion contract revenue, over $500 million net revenue, and more than $140 million EBITDA. The $120 million Mantis Innovation acquisition closed October 30, adding roughly $75 million in net revenue for 2026.

Unity reported Q3 FY2026 strategic revenue of $597M, up 59% YoY, with Strategic Grow of $432M (+90% YoY) driven by Vector revenue growing 126% YoY and 40% QoQ, roughly double the guided 20% sequential growth. Adjusted EBITDA was $257M at a 41% margin, up 1,800 bps YoY, and the company posted its first GAAP profit since IPO at $122M net income (20% margin), with record free cash flow of $220M and a $2.65B cash balance. Q4 guidance calls for strategic revenue of $683-691M (+65-67% YoY), Grow growth of 105-107% and adjusted EBITDA of $290-295M (42% margin), implying further acceleration from Q3.

Unusual Machines reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $13.9 million, up 551% year-over-year but down sequentially from $16.7 million in Q2, with a 35.4% gross margin and an adjusted EBITDA loss of roughly $700,000. GAAP net loss was about $25 million ($0.50 per share), driven mainly by $5.5 million in non-cash stock compensation and $18.4 million in unrealized losses on short-term investments. Q4 revenue guidance was maintained at $25 million, matching the target set last quarter, and management said it is nearly fully allocated through Q1 2027. Inventory and prepaid inventory rose to $65.9 million from $42.4 million, and cash stood at $162 million with $98.4 million in short-term investments.

US Foods reported Q3 net sales up 2.1% to $10.4 billion on total case volume growth of 1.3%, with adjusted EBITDA up 9.9% to $555 million (margin +38 bps to 5.3%) and adjusted diluted EPS up 17.8% to $1.26. Independent restaurant case growth held at 5% and net new accounts improved to 5.5%, but total volume growth came in below management's expectations as the macro backdrop deteriorated and lower center-of-the-plate inflation cut 100-150 bps from sales. FY2026 guidance was tightened rather than raised (net sales +4-5%, adjusted EBITDA +9-11%, adjusted EPS +18-20%), with Q4 carrying roughly one point of watching-cost headwind and 1-1.5 points of fuel headwind. Management flagged Prime Line ($110 million annual sales), $191 million of Q3 buybacks ($690 million YTD), and AI initiatives now generating over $75 million of adjusted EBITDA, ramping to $110 million next year.

Revenue rose 13% to $223 million with PT visits up 8%, adjusted EPS of $0.80 up $0.14, and EBITDA of $28 million up 16%, driven largely by hospital affiliations (revenue share from <5% in Q2 to >13% in Q3) pushing revenue per visit up $5 to $111. Adjusted PT margin expanded 60 bps to 19% despite a ~150 bps drag from self-insured employee health claims, which were $7 million higher year-to-date and $2 million over budget in Q3. Full-year EBITDA guidance of $102-106 million was reaffirmed, not raised, and no 2027 numerical guidance was provided. Management flagged continued elevated benefit costs into Q4 while noting a final CMS rule that follows its IPCI modifier phase-out context as a multi-year tailwind.

Energy Fuels reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $29.2 million, including $28.7 million and $17.9 million of gross profit (about 63% margin) from uranium, with 320,000 lbs sold at an $88.90/lb realized price versus a ~$34/lb cost. The quarter produced a $52.2 million net loss, or $0.20 per share, driven mainly by $35.3 million of non-cash mark-to-market losses on marketable securities plus $9 million of ASM/VAC transaction costs. Guidance was not raised: the company said it hit the low end of full-year processed-pound guidance, targets the low end of sales guidance (1.5 million lbs), and is only 'hopeful' of reaching the low end of mining guidance after Pinyon Plain grades of 1.04% came in below expectations. Strategic milestones (ASM close, VAC pending, Donald conditional AUD 180 million debt commitment) advanced, but no near-term ASM financial contribution is expected.

Vericel reported Q3 revenue of $85.4 million, up 26% YoY and well above guidance, with MACI at $67.4 million (+21%) and burn care at a record $18 million (+52%). GAAP net income rose 179% to $14.2 million ($0.27 per diluted share), adjusted EBITDA grew 48% to $25.2 million at a 30% margin, and free cash flow was $16 million. Full-year revenue guidance was raised to $344-346 million from $330-340 million, the third consecutive raise, with MACI raised to $290-292 million and burn care to approximately $54 million, and adjusted EBITDA margin guidance lifted to approximately 28% from 27%.

Victory Capital reported Q3 revenue of $396.6 million, up 10% YoY and its second highest ever, with adjusted EPS of $1.98 up 21% and adjusted EBITDA margin of 53.5%, up 80 bps YoY and above the 50% long-term guide. Record long-term net inflows of $11.7 billion (13.8% annualized organic growth) and record gross flows of $30.5 billion drove total client assets to a record $355.5 billion, up 3% QoQ and 13% YoY. The 46-47 bps full-year fee rate guidance was reiterated (46.3 bps YTD) despite a Q3 dip to 44.8 bps from annual-fee timing, and the First Eagle deal remains on track to close by end-Q1 2027 with $280 million net expense synergy and 35% accretion targets unchanged. Management said Q3 flow momentum has continued into Q4.

First commercial quarter for TRUTAKNA generated $10.3M in net product revenue on a partial quarter following July 7 accelerated approval, with roughly 700 Patient Start Forms to date; management noted about half of Q3 sales were inventory stocking versus demand. Cost of sales was $3.3M, R&D fell to $41.3M from $56.5M on manufacturing capitalization, SG&A rose to $61.4M from $27.5M on launch investment, and net loss widened to $93.7M ($1.30/share) from $80.3M ($1.26). The company submitted an sBLA for full approval based on ORIGIN 3 final efficacy (76% risk reduction in kidney progression, HR 0.24) targeting a mid-2027 FDA decision, with an EU MAA planned for Q1 2027. Cash was $384M at quarter-end, rising to $459M pro forma after a $75M October draw, with up to $350M remaining under the facility.

Virtu reported Q3 FY2026 Adjusted Net Trading Income of $704 million ($11 million/day), Adjusted EBITDA of $438 million at a 62% margin, and Adjusted EPS of $1.77. Market Making ANTI was $9 million/day, down only about 4% sequentially despite U.S. equity volumes down mid-teens and realized volatility down more than 20%. Trailing-twelve-month ANTI per day of $11.3 million, Adjusted EBITDA of $1.8 billion, and Adjusted EPS of $7.69 were all-time highs. Management maintained the $0.24 quarterly dividend, cited a 23% cash comp ratio and 1.4x debt-to-EBITDA, and did not provide formal forward guidance.

Aurora Networks Q3 FY2026 net sales were $320 million, down 5% YoY, while adjusted EBITDA rose to $57 million (up 5%) and adjusted EPS rose 283% to $0.23, aided by lower variable compensation. Management lowered full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $180-200 million, citing customer amplifier order pushouts into 2027 and a roughly $40 million annual memory chip cost impact, with 2027 specifics deferred. The quarter included large capital returns: a $1.50/share special distribution (~$300 million), 28.9 million shares repurchased (~13% of shares) for $225 million, and a new $100 million buyback authorization. CEO Chuck Treadway also announced he will step down February 1.

VieMed reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $80.7 million, up 12.2% YoY and 3.3% sequentially, with net income of $4.6 million ($0.11 per diluted share) up 32% YoY and about 68% QoQ. Adjusted EBITDA was $17.1 million (21.1% margin), up 6% YoY and 24% sequentially but down from 22.4% a year ago as mix shifted toward lower-margin sales and services. Full-year revenue guidance was raised at the low end to $316-$320 million from $314-$320 million, but Adjusted EBITDA guidance was narrowed to $64-$66 million from $64-$68 million, cutting the top end. Ventilator rental revenue grew 7.4% YoY to $37.5 million and PAP patients rose 37.5% YoY, while free cash flow was only $4 million on AR timing and audit-related collection delays management expects to reverse in Q4.

Vivmark Residential's inaugural quarter reported Q3 Core FFO of $1.03/share, reflecting AVB as accounting acquirer before the Aug 17 merger close and the combined company after it. Full-year same-store revenue guidance was raised 20 bps to 2.2%, and projected gross synergies were lifted to $185M (net $135M) from $175M/$125M, with merger costs cut to $725M from $750M and run-rate accretion rising to ~3% from 2%. Q4 Core FFO guidance is $1.03/share at the midpoint, and 2027 building blocks include ~1% embedded same-store revenue growth, ~$70M incremental development NOI and ~150 bps of development contribution to Core FFO growth. Blended rate change was 3.1% in Q3 (up 150 bps YoY), occupancy just under 96%, and turnover fell 50 bps to 12.7%.

Vontier reported Q3 sales of $737 million with ~6% core growth versus a 5% guide, and adjusted operating margin of just over 24%, up 300 bps versus an ~110 bps guide. Full-year revenue guidance midpoint was raised to ~$3.03 billion (~3% core), full-year margin expansion raised to ~180 bps, and adjusted EPS raised to $3.60-$3.64, above the prior high end. Q3 also included ~$4 million of favorable geographic/product mix that management said will not repeat, and Q4 core growth steps down to ~3% with Mobility Technologies flattish. Structural cost savings now track ~$20 million versus $15 million originally, and the company repurchased ~3 million shares for $80 million in the quarter.

Verisk reported Q3 revenue of $809 million, up 5% GAAP and 7.4% on an organic constant-currency basis, with underwriting up 7.7% and claims up 6.7%. Subscription revenue grew 8.2% OCC (84% of total) while transactional revenue rose 3.2%, which management said was modestly ahead of expectations on data overages and Life Solutions services it does not expect to repeat in Q4. Total adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 90 bps to 56.7%, adjusted EPS rose 14% to $1.96, and GAAP net income fell 3% to $219 million on investment losses and higher interest expense. Full-year guidance was maintained (revenue $3.19-3.24B, EBITDA $1.79-1.83B, adjusted EPS $7.45-7.75) but management said results likely land toward the midpoint of the range.

VSE reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $541 million, up 91% (about 17% organic), adjusted EBITDA of $107 million up 126%, a record 19.8% adjusted EBITDA margin (up ~310 bps), and adjusted diluted EPS of $2.01 up 49%. Free cash flow was ~$47 million versus $18 million a year ago, and adjusted net leverage fell to 2.3x from 2.4x. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance to 65%-66.5% from 61%-64% and adjusted EBITDA margin to 18.9%-19.1% from 18.7%-19%. Q4 revenue is guided lower sequentially on seasonality and a tough December 2025 comparison, and 2027 guidance is deferred to the December investor day.

Lightspeed reported organic revenue of $323.8M, up 15% and at the high end of the 12%-16% outlook, with software revenue up 9% (14% in growth engines), total GTV up 8% to $25.8B, gross margin of 44% vs 46% a year ago, and adjusted EBITDA of $22.7M (7.0% margin, up from $21.3M). Adjusted free cash flow was $4M versus a $4.5M outflow last quarter. Management left FY2027 guidance unchanged (revenue $1.225B-$1.265B, adjusted EBITDA $75M-$95M) and introduced Q3 guidance of $310M-$320M revenue and $25M-$30M adjusted EBITDA. The key change was a deliberate tightening of deal parameters: net new locations fell sharply to ~800 from ~2,000 in the prior-year quarter, but new locations carried 27% more software revenue, software ARPU rose 7%, and payments penetration reached 45%.

Subscription revenue rose 7.1% YoY in USD but only 0.2% FX-neutral, GMV grew 12.0% in USD and 4.5% FX-neutral, both decelerating sequentially on Brazil same-store weakness. Non-GAAP operating income grew 27.1% to $12.1 million (19.0% margin, below management's own expectation on higher AI R&D usage), while non-GAAP net income fell to $7.0 million from $10.6 million on mark-to-market losses; free cash flow rose 77.3% to $13.3 million. Q4 guidance calls for negative low-single-digit FX-neutral subscription revenue growth, and the full year is revised to roughly flat FX-neutral subscription revenue from prior expectations, reflecting further Brazil consumption weakening seen in October. Management attributed the revision to volume and macro, not churn, win rates, or pricing, and declined to extrapolate Q4 into 2027.

Viatris reported Q3 FY2026 total revenues of $3.75 billion, described as in line with expectations, with adjusted EBITDA of $1.2 billion and adjusted EPS of $0.71; North America grew ~7% and Greater China ~10%, while adjusted gross margin came in above expectations at 58%. Management narrowed and raised the midpoint of 2026 guidance across all key metrics (operational growth ~2% revenue, ~6% adjusted EBITDA, ~8% adjusted EPS), excluding Pacira. Offsets included ~$100 million of Q3 supply-constraint impact from Nashik (now OAI with manufacturing suspended) and an expected ~$100 million Q4 hit, while China growth is guided to slow below 10% in Q4 and toward low-to-mid single digits in 2027. The pending Pacira acquisition (tender launched October 30, close expected before end-November) is expected to be immediately accretive in 2027 and add >$1 billion of U.S. innovative medicines revenue.

Total revenue fell 20% to $539 million (down 3% excluding the hardware transition), with recurring revenue up just 1%, software up 3%, and services flat. Adjusted EBITDA was $120 million, down 2%, though margin expanded 410 bps to 22.3% on the hardware mix shift and was essentially flat ex-hardware; non-GAAP EPS rose 7% to $0.32. Management reaffirmed Adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow guidance but now expects revenue at the low end of the prior range due to delayed hardware purchases and installation revenue, and flagged continued SMB restaurant pressure with restaurant revenue down 5% ex-hardware and payment sites down 1% to 8,400. The main positive was sales momentum: RCV rose 151% YoY to $440 million (up 54% sequentially) on 10 new VCP contracts, and Aloha Next went live at Bruster's.

WaterBridge reported record produced water volumes of 2.8 MMbpd (up 6% sequentially), record revenue of $240.2 million (up 10% sequentially), and Adjusted EBITDA of $124.2 million (up 7% sequentially) at a roughly 52% margin. Management raised full-year 2026 volume guidance to 2.65-2.75 MMbpd and Adjusted EBITDA to $465-485 million (midpoints up 2% and 4%), the third consecutive raise, while narrowing CapEx to $530-560 million (midpoint down 3%) on timing shifts into 2027. Produced water handling revenue rose to $0.77/bbl from $0.72 a year ago, and the company declared a $0.05 dividend with covenant net leverage of 3.5x against a sub-3x target.

WD reported Q3 FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS of -$1.15, driven by a $49M valuation adjustment plus an $8M loss-sharing charge and $7M of REO operating costs tied to accelerated liquidation of legacy GSE loan repurchase assets; adjusted core EPS was $0.92 and adjusted EBITDA $61M. Total transaction volume fell 11% and revenue was $298M, down 12% YoY, as a 58% rise in brokered debt originations was offset by GSE and HUD originations down 55% and 29% and investment sales down 25%. Full-year guidance calls for GAAP diluted EPS of -$0.10 to $0.30, adjusted EBITDA of $260-280M, and adjusted core EPS of $4.00-4.50, implying Q4 core EPS of $0.90-1.40. Management said the GSE fraud investigations are complete with no further buybacks expected, and cost actions initiated in Q4 are expected to improve NOI by roughly $20M annually by mid-2027.

Wendy's reported Q3 FY2026 global systemwide sales down 5.9% and U.S. same-restaurant sales down 5.7%, with traffic falling 11.9% offset by average check growth of 6.2%; the U.S. comp improved 130 bps sequentially from Q2. Total adjusted revenue was $435.6 million (down 1.6%), adjusted EBITDA fell $24.6 million to $113.4 million, and adjusted EPS was $0.13, with G&A up $15.2 million including $11.9 million of Dave's Way investment and a $9.1 million doubtful-accounts charge for franchisee deferrals. Management gave no formal forward guidance beyond stating Q4 has started with early improvement and that trajectory details will come on the next call; net debt leverage was 5.2x. Key changes versus prior period: a location-optional breakfast strategy worth up to $200 million in restaurant-level EBITDA, an LOI to acquire up to 163 Meritage restaurants, and rejection of an unsolicited acquisition offer.

WES reported Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $708 million, up 12% YoY but down modestly sequentially, with DCF of $512 million and net income to limited partners of $325 million. Partnership-wide natural gas throughput hit a record 5.9 Bcf/d (up 8% sequentially, Delaware up 20%), and produced water set another Delaware record. Management now expects full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA above the midpoint of its already-raised $2.75-$2.95 billion range, with DCF and FCF guidance ranges unchanged and 2027 capex expected in line with 2026. The quarter's sequential softness came from West Texas contract mix and pricing, DJ Basin declines, lower NGL/skim oil, and seasonal O&M, partially offset by a full quarter of Brazos.

Westrock reported record Q3 FY2026 consolidated adjusted EBITDA of $26.4 million, up ~14% YoY, with nine-month EBITDA of $73.7 million up 58%. Net sales of ~$300 million fell 15.4% YoY, driven by ~$26 million in tariff refunds recorded as a sales reduction, lower green coffee pass-through, and the prior single-serve customer loss; excluding tariffs, sales were ~$326 million.
