Operating profit swung to $3.2 million from an $8.6 million loss, and the company reaffirmed FY2026 EBITDA guidance of $90-100 million (current estimate $95 million, +36%) while initiating a 2027 outlook of ~$130 million EBITDA (+35% over the midpoint). It closed a $600 million upsized credit facility maturing 2031 and repurchased $40 million of convertible notes.

Revenue rose to $26.6M from $25.3M in Q2 and $24.3M a year ago, but GAAP net income of $3.1M ($0.34/share) fell from $3.7M ($0.41) in Q3 2025 and Economic Earnings declined to $4.4M ($0.48) from $5.7M ($0.64) year over year, with $1.7M of severance and higher taxes offsetting revenue. Still, income nearly doubled sequentially from $1.5M ($0.17) and Economic Earnings rose from $3.0M ($0.33). Firmwide AUM/AUA was $17.1B, with AUM net outflows of $0.3B and market depreciation of $0.6B in the quarter. No formal guidance was issued; the board declared a $0.15 quarterly dividend, and management cited a robust pipeline, ETF assets of $430M at quarter-end (about $460M since), and roughly $30M of new private capital commitments.

Q3 FY2026 total revenue was $263M, up 17% YoY and $1M above the high end of guidance, with subscription revenue also up 17% to $246M. Non-GAAP operating margin reached 18.3%, 85 bps above the high end of guidance and up 560 bps YoY, while non-GAAP EPS of $0.72 (up from $0.46) reflects a newly applied 22% non-GAAP tax rate. Full-year revenue guidance of $1.041-1.044B and ~19% subscription growth remain essentially intact, with the non-GAAP operating margin outlook raised 25 bps at the midpoint to 18.2%-18.3%; management flagged that FX and sustainability tailwinds have subsided, contributing to a Q4 revenue guide that does not fully pass through the Q3 beat. CRPO grew 17% YoY (18% in constant currency), and the >$300K contract cohort grew 31%.

Unisys reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $472 million, up 2.5% YoY as reported and 0.6% in constant currency, about $20 million above the prior outlook, with TS&S at $387 million (vs. $370 million expected) and ClearPath at $84 million (vs. ~$80 million expected). Non-GAAP operating margin of 7.2% came in well above the ~4% guided, up 180 bps YoY, and GAAP operating profit was $24 million versus a prior-year loss that included a $55 million goodwill impairment. Full-year revenue guidance was raised for the second time this year to a constant-currency decline of 3% to 1.5% from 5% to 3.5%, while non-GAAP operating margin guidance of 9%-11% and free cash flow of about negative $25 million were reiterated. New business TCV rose 78% YoY and total TCV 43% YoY, but free cash flow was negative $58 million versus positive $20 million a year ago and the GAAP net loss was $201 million on a $151 million non-cash pension settlement charge.

TXRH reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.6 billion, up 9.5% YoY, with same-store sales +4.3% (0.7% traffic) and diluted EPS +8.6% to $1.36; restaurant margin expanded 30 bps to 14.6%. Comps decelerated sharply to 1.0% in September (after 5.9% and 6.8% in July/August) on a social media hoax and softer trends; Q4-to-date comps are +1.5%, with management noting sequential weekly improvement. FY2026 commodity inflation guidance held at ~5% (Q4 improved to ~4.5%), labor narrowed to 3.5%-4%, capex raised to ~$440M, and initial FY2027 guides set at ~4% commodity, ~3% labor, and ~$425M capex.

Revenue was essentially flat at $320 million with adjusted operating income of $50 million (-2%), a 15.7% margin (down 30 bps), and adjusted EPS of $1.69 (+4%) driven by a lower share count; free cash flow rose 8% to $137 million through nine months. Strength in ETS (revenue +12% to $43 million, margin +80 bps to 42.5%) and healthcare enrollment (+9%, now 54% of U.S. Higher Education) was offset by Australia, where enrollment fell 9% and a $134 million non-cash goodwill/intangibles impairment was recorded. Management said full-year results will likely fall outside the notional outlook, guided 2027 revenue to roughly flat with negligible margin expansion, and plans ~$50 million in incremental growth investments. Australia's international visa approvals slowed sharply, at times down 80% year over year, and the government closed the onshore transfer market.

10X Genomics reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $150.7 million, up 1% year-over-year, as consumables grew 5% (spatial +16%, single-cell +1%) while total instrument revenue fell 43%. Gross margin expanded to 75% from 67% a year ago on lower inventory write-downs and mix, and the company raised its full-year 2026 revenue outlook to $625-635 million from $610-630 million. Management also lifted its Atera shipment expectation to ~50 units by year-end from ~40, but guided Q4 gross margin down to the low-to-mid 60s as Atera instrument shipments ramp and flagged lower margins for 2027 amid an instrument-heavy year.

Normalized FFO was $43.8 million ($0.34/share), up 29.3% YoY, and Adjusted EBITDAre was $133.5 million, both above consensus; retained-hotel RevPAR rose 8.3% to $128.38 and Adjusted Hotel EBITDA grew 16.2% with 130 bps of margin expansion to 15.4%. Guidance was mixed: RevPAR outlook was raised for retained and Exit Hotels and a new $96 million (plus ~$13 million from CBRE-based RevPAR growth) operating upside plan targets ~20% retained-hotel margins, but the hotel EBITDA range high end was cut to $124-$134 million on a $3.8 million James Nautilus delay and Exit Hotel underperformance, and net lease NOI guidance fell to $373-$379 million. Full-year Normalized FFO is guided to $1.07-$1.22 per share and CAD turned positive on a rolling four-quarter basis from an $83 million deficit a year ago. The board unanimously rejected TKO LLC's unsolicited $2 billion hotel-portfolio proposal as significantly undervaluing the assets.

Savers Value Village reported Q3 net sales up 8.5% to $463 million (8.9% constant currency) with comps +4.2%, U.S. net sales +12.2% on a 5.9% comp, and Canada net sales +2.5% with comps +1.5%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 8% to $76 million (16.4% of sales), gross margin expanded 100 bps to 43.1% on COGS, GAAP EPS was $0.15 and adjusted EPS $0.16. Full-year guidance was updated to net sales of $1.77-$1.78 billion, comps of 3.5%-4.0%, and Adjusted EBITDA of $270-$275 million, with Q4 revenue roughly flat (up mid-to-high single digits excluding last year's 53rd week) and comps modestly below Q3 as the company laps an 8.8% U.S. comp. Management reiterated the 50-100 bps annual EBITDA margin expansion framework beginning in 2027, with 2027 at the low end (~50 bps), and disclosed ~$10 million of annualized labor savings from the new Autotagger upon full deployment by early 2028, requiring ~$40 million of CapEx.

Molson Coors reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated net sales revenue of $2.9 billion, down 1.2% YoY, underlying pre-tax income of $349 million, down 17.4%, and underlying EPS of $1.46, down 12.6%. The company cut full-year 2026 guidance across all key metrics: NSR now expected -1% to -2% (vs. prior flat +/-1%), underlying pre-tax income -21% to -24% (vs. prior -15% to -18%), underlying EPS -16% to -19% (vs. prior -11% to -15%), and underlying free cash flow to $1 billion +/-10% (vs. prior $1.1 billion +/-10%). Management cited U.S. category softness (industry down more than 4%), increased U.K. promotional activity, elevated Midwest Premium and aluminum costs, and a tighter freight market, with Midwest Premium alone driving roughly $30 million of YoY cost increase in the quarter and expected to add approximately $130 million for the full year (about 10 points of pre-tax income impact, or more than $0.50 of EPS).

Revenue returned to growth at $84.7 million, up 5.3% YoY, but gross margin fell to 34.9% from 37.4% on product mix and higher promotional, tariff and freight costs, and Adjusted EBITDA dropped to $8.1 million from $11 million. GAAP net income rose to $4.4 million ($0.24/diluted share) from $1.7 million ($0.08), helped by $1.9 million of prior-year debt extinguishment and current-quarter insurance recoveries. Full-year 2026 guidance was reaffirmed at $335-355 million revenue and $44-48 million Adjusted EBITDA, requiring a substantial Q4 that management ties to retailer holiday replenishment shifted out of Q3, new products and major releases including GTA VI. Retailers bought only to normal seasonal levels in Q3, pushing holiday load-in into Q4, while October watch-through and orders accelerated; inventory rose ~$23.2 million sequentially to $79.8 million and no shares were repurchased after ~$25 million in Q2.

Adjusted net investment income was $0.15 per share against a $0.17 quarterly dividend, with total investment income of $28.5 million ($0.34/share). NAV fell $0.97 per share to $5.61, of which $0.68 came from the previously disclosed portfolio sale to a Pantheon-sponsored continuation vehicle. Non-accruals rose to 14.2% at cost and 3.4% at fair value from 7.4% and 1.6%, and net realized losses were $75.8 million ($0.91/share). Management declared a $0.17 Q4 dividend, kept $253 million in cash and 0.16x net leverage, and declined to give any timeline or detail on the KBW-assisted strategic review.

Total Q3 revenue fell 7.4% to $519.2 million (-5.8% same-store), adjusted EBITDA dropped 36% to $36.6 million, and digital advertising declined 13.9% on search-driven pressure in indirect programmatic revenue. Digital-only subscription revenue grew 5.3% to $46 million with record ARPU of $10.82 (+23%), and digital other revenue rose 24.8% to $21.3 million. Full-year same-store revenue guidance was cut to a mid-single-digit decline from a prior low-single-digit decline, with the 50% digital revenue mix target pushed to 2027 and full-year adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow now expected to decline versus 2025. Management implemented a $100 million annualized cost reduction program in late Q3 and guided to significant sequential EBITDA and free cash flow improvement in Q4.

Q3 revenue was $399 million at the high end of the outlook, recurring revenue $359 million also at the high end, and non-GAAP EPS of $0.70 beat the top of the range by $0.11. Total ARR grew 1% (2% constant currency) and cloud ARR grew 11%, while Q3 recurring revenue declined year-over-year against a first-half-skewed linearity comparison. FY26 revenue range was narrowed to the high end (-1% to 0%), recurring revenue to 1%-2%, and EPS guidance raised to $2.86-$2.90 with operating margin expansion now seen at ~200 bps versus 100 bps expected at the start of the year. Q4 guidance calls for recurring revenue down 2%-4% and total revenue down 4%-6% on upfront-recognition timing.

Q3 revenue was approximately $235 million, down 26% year-over-year, with ex-TAC gross profit of $93.5 million, down 28% and decelerating from a 6% decline in Q2. Enterprise ex-TAC gross profit fell 14% (North America -15%, EMEA weak in August, APAC +5%) while direct response/SME ex-TAC gross profit fell 50% on AI-summary and algorithm-driven page view declines of 20% to 60%. Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $8.1 million, a $272 million non-cash goodwill impairment was recorded, and free cash flow before interest was -$1.4 million ($33 million total cash use including $31 million semi-annual interest). No formal guidance was given; management said early Q4 shows some recovery versus Q3 on operational improvements and seasonality, and that it is further scrutinizing costs and capital structure.

Teleflex reported Q3 2026 revenue of $567.8 million, up 0.2% GAAP and 3.0% pro forma adjusted constant currency, with adjusted operating margin of 25% (up 300 bps) and adjusted EPS of $2.63, up 39.2% year over year and ahead of expectations. Vascular grew 4.6% and Surgical 5.1%, while Interventional returned to positive growth at 0.2% as integration disruptions eased. Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $7.50-$7.75 from $6.90-$7.20, including a $0.31 IEEPA tariff refund benefit, while pro forma constant currency revenue growth guidance was maintained at 3.5%-4.5%. The company repurchased about $350 million of shares since July 1, $100 million more than previously announced, and noted the Acute Care and Interventional Urology divestiture may slip into 2027 pending FTC review.

Taseko (TGB) reported Q3 F2026 revenue of CAD 342 million, up 100% YoY, with Adjusted EBITDA of CAD 161 million (a quarterly record) and cash flow from operations of CAD 122 million; consolidated copper sales were 37.4 million pounds. 2026 production guidance was raised by 5 million pounds to 115-120 million pounds, but management guided Q4 lower due to the transition to oxidized ore at Gibraltar, with recoveries averaging 77% and costs at $2.72/lb. Florence Copper produced 7 million pounds (up 35% QoQ) and C1 costs fell 25% to $3.54/lb, though sulfuric acid costs are expected to rise next year and leverage remains about 1x net debt/EBITDA.

Tecnoglass reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $310.6 million, up 19.2% year-over-year, but adjusted EBITDA fell to $47.7 million from $79.1 million and gross margin contracted to 34.1% from 42.7%. The decline was driven by roughly 580 bps of peso impact (including an $8.4 million non-cash inventory revaluation), a 52% year-over-year rise in aluminum prices, Section 232 tariffs that added about $15.5 million of SG&A, and Colombia's 23% minimum wage increase. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $1.1-$1.14 billion, but adjusted EBITDA guidance was cut to $210-$220 million, reflecting the $8.4 million non-cash item; management said Q3 was the margin low point and expects sequential gross margin improvement in Q4 toward the high-30s, with 2027 margins better still.

TIC reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $640 million, up 12.5% year-over-year (13.0% constant currency, 8.4% organic), with adjusted EBITDA up 19% to $107 million and margin expanding roughly 90 bps to 16.8%. Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.18, up from $0.14 in Q2, and all three segments grew, led by C&E at +20.3% to a record $223 million and I&M returning to growth at +8.5%. The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $2.24-2.27 billion from $2.15-2.25 billion and narrowed adjusted EBITDA to $342-350 million, raising the midpoint to $346 million. GeoVerra, WDI, and Core Group acquisitions were announced adding roughly $90 million annualized revenue; geospatial margins fell 330 bps on project mix and pass-through work despite revenue growth.

Millicom reported Q3 2026 service revenue of $2.1 billion, up 6.1% reported and 5.4% organically (fourth consecutive mid-single-digit organic quarter), with adjusted EBITDA at a record $1.1 billion, up 7.7% organically at a 48% margin despite ~$30 million of severance. Equity free cash flow reached $316 million, up ~30% YoY, bringing nine-month EFCF to ~$870 million and leverage down to 2.53. Full-year guidance was maintained at ~$1.1 billion EFCF and sub-2.5x leverage, though management flagged Q4 margin moderation in Ecuador and continued home subscriber pressure. Key changes versus prior periods include the completed Colombia brand consolidation with a four-year investment plan, an Ecuador brand launch, a Guatemala litigation settlement, and home net losses of 86,000 driven by the Colombia earthquake and the deliberate more-for-more pricing strategy.

TransMedics reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $203M, up 41% YoY (organic $194M, up 35%), the highest quarterly revenue in company history, with product revenue of $113M (+29%) and service revenue of $90M (+60%). Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.51 and adjusted operating margin 14.2%. Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $764M-$774M from $737M-$757M (26%-28% growth), inclusive of ~$14M from PAD Aviation, while the adjusted operating margin range of 12.5%-14% was maintained and no contribution from ENHANCE Part B or DENOVO is assumed.

Q3 revenue rose 14% YoY to $284 million with pump shipments up 12% to ~33,000 and gross margin of 57%, up nearly 3 points YoY; U.S. sales grew 9% to $191 million and international hit a record $93 million, up 26%. Adjusted EBITDA reached 6% of sales, the fifth consecutive positive quarter, with operating margin up 8 points and $443 million in cash. Full-year 2026 guidance was maintained at $1.065-1.085 billion with gross margin of 56%-57%, but management said pharmacy adoption is tracking well below earlier plans (10%-12% of the year versus prior assumptions), expects continued sales headwinds into 2027, and framed 2027 growth as mid-to-high single digits versus ~12% consensus. The quarter also included CEO succession, with John Sheridan retiring at end-2026 and Jeannette Bankes named incoming CEO effective November 16.

TPL reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of ~$273 million, up 11% sequentially and 35% YoY, an all-time high, with net income of $167 million ($2.42/diluted share, +38% YoY), adjusted EBITDA of $238 million at an 87% margin, and free cash flow of $170 million (+39% YoY). Oil production of 17.1 Mbbl/d and total production of 42.3 Mboe/d were quarterly records, produced water royalty volumes hit a record 5.5 million bbl/d (+14% sequential, +27% YoY), and SLIM revenue rose 53% sequentially to $36 million. No formal guidance was issued; management flagged a decline in net line-of-sight wells to 16.8 and water sales roughly flat sequentially, but said the Q4 completion schedule is more robust and the next couple of quarters should be stronger. The prior-period change is the third consecutive quarter of record revenue, net income, and free cash flow.

Q3 FY2026 net income was $3.3 million, or $0.12 per share, up from $1.7 million/$0.06, and adjusted EBITDA nearly doubled to $10.4 million from $5.3 million, but results were heavily aided by $3.9 million of crop insurance proceeds, $2.6 million of pistachio bonus pricing, and an early harvest that pulled wine grape sales forward. Trailing twelve-month adjusted EBITDA reached $35 million, up 44% from $24.3 million, though management repeatedly flagged that land-sale timing and farming items will not repeat. No formal forward guidance was issued; the CEO instead outlined a multi-part plan to cut costs and CapEx and convert land to recurring income, with details deferred. Shareholder questions centered on negative free cash flow, rising net debt, and the share-price discount to intrinsic value, which management acknowledged while defending the quarter's cash improvement.

Targa reported Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $1.5B, 6% lower than Q2 as record Permian G&P, NGL transportation (1.17 MMBbl/d) and fractionation (1.26 MMBbl/d) volumes were offset by lower marketing/optimization and LPG exports. Management raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to at least $6B, more than 21% above 2025, and pointed to multiple years of double-digit Permian volume growth. Permian volumes hit a record 7.5 Bcf/d, up 5% sequentially and 14% YoY, with several plants (Copperhead, Yeti, Yeti II, Train 12, Bull Run Extension) starting ahead of schedule and a new Train 14 fractionator announced. Capital returns were reinforced by a $1.25 quarterly dividend (up 25% YoY) and an intended 20% increase to $6/share in 2027, alongside $187M of YTD buybacks.

TripAdvisor reported Q3 FY2026 consolidated revenue of $436 million, down 11% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of $71 million (16% of revenue). Experiences revenue fell 3% with segment EBITDA down 440 bps to 13% of revenue, while Hotels and Other revenue dropped 23% to $152 million and segment EBITDA fell ~650 bps to 22%. Management guided Q4 group revenue to decline in the low teens and group adjusted EBITDA margins to step down to low-to-mid single digits, with Experiences EBITDA roughly break-even. The quarter included a $369 million goodwill impairment in H&O, a global restructuring targeting ~$40 million in group annualized savings, and the announced CEO and CFO departures.

Q3 FY2026 medical-only revenue of $230 million rose 4% YoY and 4% QoQ versus medical-only baselines of $221 million and $222 million, exceeding guidance and outperforming seasonal trends on Georgia and Pennsylvania growth. Gross margin was 64%, up ~1 point YoY and sequentially, adjusted EBITDA was $89 million (39% margin), and operating cash flow was $74 million against $29 million of capex for $45 million free cash flow; net income was only $1 million, or $18 million / $0.09 per share excluding non-recurring items. Q4 revenue guidance is up low single digits sequentially with gross margin comparable to recent quarters but pressured by holiday promotions, and purchase accounting from the Harvest deconsolidation is expected to drive a fourth-quarter net loss; FY2026 operating cash flow is guided to at least $225 million while capex rises to ~$105 million from ~$95 million. Prior framing on 280E is unchanged, with the uncertain tax position covering 2019 to present including $102 million of IRS refunds and interest.

Tronox reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $827 million, up 18% YoY, driven by higher TiO2 volumes (+10%) and prices (+9%), with adjusted EBITDA of $101 million at a 12.2% margin. Adjusted diluted EPS was a loss of $0.34, and net loss attributable to Tronox was $55 million. Q4 guidance calls for adjusted EBITDA of $80–90 million, reflecting $15–20 million of higher raw material costs from the prolonged Middle East conflict, and TiO2 volumes down high-single to low-double digits sequentially. Full-year free cash flow is now expected to be a use of $25–50 million, versus prior expectations, with capex cut by roughly $30 million.

TC Energy reported Q3 FY2026 comparable EBITDA above $3 billion, up 13% YoY, with comparable EPS of $0.94, up 22%, and year-to-date comparable EBITDA of $9 billion, also up 13%. All four segments grew, led by U.S. natural gas pipelines up 17% and Power and Energy Solutions up 35% on 97% Bruce Power availability and a full quarter of Unit 3 contributions. Management raised 2026 comparable EBITDA guidance to $11.8-$12 billion (a $200 million increase) and set 2027 at $12.3-$12.5 billion versus the prior $11.7-$11.9 billion outlook, alongside a new 2031 outlook of 5%-7% annual EBITDA growth, 3%-5% dividend growth, and debt-to-EBITDA exiting 2026 at 4.55x-4.6x. The company announced $3 billion of new projects, bringing sanctioned and pending approval spend to $30 billion, with over $40 billion in origination.

Q3 FY2026 total revenue was $405.6 million, up 11% YoY, with subscription revenue up 14% to $287.9 million and total subscription pets up 6% to 1.145 million. Adjusted operating income hit an all-time high of $47 million (up 15%), subscription AOI was $45.4 million at a 15.8% margin, net income was $9.3 million or $0.21 per share, and free cash flow reached a record $28.5 million. FY2026 revenue guidance was narrowed to $1.59-1.597 billion and total AOI guidance to $179-182 million, with the subscription revenue midpoint rising to 14% YoY growth; Q4 revenue is guided to $407-414 million. Net new pets rose over 28% YoY, retention improved for a seventh consecutive quarter to 98.38%, and the company repurchased roughly $25 million of shares during the quarter.

Q3 FY2026 sales reached $3.1 billion, up 4% YoY and 5% sequentially, with EBITDA up 16% sequentially to $756 million at a 24% margin. Management guided Q4 revenue up close to 10% sequentially with EBITDA margin around 25%, citing higher volumes across most markets and a positive U.S. pricing dynamic from Pipe Logix (+8-9% in Q3, +6% in October). U.S. OCTG demand rose roughly 15% since the start of the conflict and tariffs are now running at $140-150 million per quarter versus the prior $120 million. Free cash flow was $168 million with net cash rising to $3.8 billion, and the company expects further volume growth in Q1 2027 with margins at or above 25%.

Total Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 20% YoY to $50.1 million, with record systems integration revenue up 75% to $16.1 million (32% of revenue vs 22% a year ago) and adjusted EBITDA up 225% to $4.7 million. Gross margin expanded 610 bps to 17.2% and net income swung to $1.1 million ($0.04 per diluted share) from a $1.5 million loss. Management raised the full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA outlook to $21-$23 million and guided Q4 systems integration revenue above the Q3 level, with growth continuing into 2027. Procurement returned to its $20-$40 million range at $32.4 million (+4%), while facilities management revenue fell 30% YoY to $1.1 million.

Verastem reported Q3 FY2026 net product revenue of $24.0 million for the AVMAPKI/FAKZYNJA CO-PACK, up 114% year over year but with new patient starts moderating after significant Q2 growth, which management attributed to late-summer seasonality; refills drove the quarter. Adjusted net loss widened to $72.8 million ($0.72 per diluted share) from $39.1 million ($0.53) a year earlier on R&D of $68.8 million and SG&A of $26.5 million. No quantitative revenue or EPS guidance was given; the only stated financial outlook is that SG&A will remain roughly flat in Q4, and cash plus roughly $250 million raised in October is expected to fund operations into the first half of 2028. Development news dominated: the new blister-pack NDA was accepted with priority review (PDUFA February 2027), VS-7375 showed a 50% confirmed ORR in second-line PDAC, and the company plans to start the phase III TARGET-D 301 first-line PDAC trial by year-end 2026.

National Grid reported H1 FY2027 underlying operating profit of GBP 2.6bn (+13% YoY) and underlying EPS of GBP 0.365 (+22%), with capital investment up 32% to a record GBP 6.7bn. Full-year capital investment guidance was upgraded to GBP 13.5bn and EPS growth guidance nudged up to 15%-16% from a prior 13%-15%, though operating cash flow growth guidance was cut to 15% from 20% on higher capex and interest. The interim dividend rose 3.8% to GBP 0.1697 per share and the five-year 8%-10% EPS CAGR and GBP 70bn capex framework were reiterated, with 80% of the programme now under supply-chain mechanisms and net debt up GBP 4.5bn to GBP 48.6bn.

Perimeter Group reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $223.5 million, up 20% YoY, on net sales of $389.9 million, which fell 24% (prior-year sales included a large one-time item). Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.85 versus $0.82, and GAAP net income was $304.5 million ($1.74/diluted share). Fire Safety EBITDA rose 14% to $201.6 million at a 64.5% margin, essentially flat YoY despite the federal retardant pricing step-down, while Specialty Products EBITDA more than doubled to $21.9 million from $9.1 million. Management guided Q4 Specialty Products EBITDA only modestly below its year-to-date quarterly average despite near-zero PDI contribution, and reiterated unchanged long-term cash flow assumptions, with net debt leverage down to 2.7x from 3.1x.

NREF reported a net loss of $0.65 per diluted share and earnings available for distribution of $0.52 per diluted share in Q3 FY2026, compared to $1.14 and $0.51 respectively in the prior year period. Cash available for distribution was $0.60 per share, exceeding the regular dividend of $0.50 per share. Management noted that both Earnings Available for Distribution (EAD) and Cash Available for Distribution (CAD) came in ahead of guidance.

Novavax reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $68 million, a decrease from $70 million in the prior year, driven by reduced R&D reimbursement offset by product sales growth and a $125 million milestone. The company raised its full-year 2026 adjusted revenue guidance to a midpoint of $400 million (range $385M-$415M) and improved expense guidance to a midpoint of $385 million. Management highlighted strong execution, including the initiation of Sanofi's Phase III trial in Europe and continued commercial momentum for Nuvaxovid.

Park Hotels & Resorts reported Q3 FY2026 results with RevPAR increasing 8.4% year-over-year to $201 and hotel adjusted EBITDA rising 8% to $135 million. Management raised full-year guidance, updating the RevPAR outlook midpoint by 200 basis points to a range of 5.5%-6.0% and increasing adjusted EBITDA guidance by approximately $13 million at the midpoint to $635-$645 million. The quarter was driven by broad-based strength across the portfolio, including record performance at Orlando Bonnet Creek and significant recovery in Hawaii despite weather disruptions.

Park-Ohio reported record Q3 FY2026 consolidated revenues of $459 million, a 15% year-over-year increase and 4% sequential growth, alongside a gross margin expansion of 120 basis points to 9.5%. Management raised full-year sales guidance to $1.75-$1.77 billion and adjusted EPS guidance to $3.35-$3.50 per share, citing strong demand in aerospace, defense, semiconductor, and AI data center markets. The company expects Q4 free cash flow to be significant as working capital levels normalize.

Consolidated revenue grew 9% to $31.7 million, driven by Honey Birdette (up 12%) and China licensing (up nearly 40%). Operating income nearly tripled to $4 million as the company achieved its seventh consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA. Management announced an agreement to acquire a Miami Beach property for a private members club, choosing this capital deployment over share repurchases.

Nu Skin reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $311 million and adjusted EPS of $0.10, both within the previously issued guidance range. Gross margin contracted to 65% from 70.5% in the prior year due to revenue mix shifts between core and Rhyz businesses. Management reiterated full-year adjusted EPS guidance of $0.55-$0.65 while noting ongoing pressures in the core business.

Natera reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $794 million, up approximately 34% year-over-year (north of 40% excluding true-ups), driven by a record 1.1 million tests processed and strong growth in oncology MRD volumes which rose 56%. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $3.005-$3.035 billion, increasing the midpoint by approximately $140 million compared to prior guidance. The company also set a long-term goal to double revenues to $6 billion by 2029.

Palomar Holdings reported a strong Q3 FY2026 with gross written premium increasing 28% year-over-year to $767 million and adjusted net income growing 47% to $81.3 million. Management raised full-year adjusted net income guidance to $280-$285 million from the prior range of $270-$280 million, citing strong execution and business evolution. The company also initiated a dividend of $0.45 per share and repurchased $8.9 million of stock during the quarter.

Planet Fitness reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $360 million (up 9% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $146.2 million (up 3.9% YoY), driven by a 1.5% system-wide same-club sales growth that beat expectations. Management raised its full-year guidance for same-club sales growth to 1.5%-2% from the prior range of 1%, while also increasing the unit opening outlook to 190-195 clubs following the acquisition of Be-Fit in Portugal. The company executed a $10 Classic Card promo test which provided regional pricing insights but confirmed no nationwide rollback, with Black Card price increases planned for Q2 2027.

Nutrien reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $1.31 billion and raised full-year guidance for both potash sales volumes (to 14.3-14.8 million tons) and nitrogen sales volumes (to 9.3-9.7 million tons). Retail adjusted EBITDA was revised down to a range of $1.72-$1.85 billion due to intentional volume reductions in Brazil and weather impacts, though the company reiterated mid-single-digit annual growth expectations for the business. Management highlighted record potash volumes, strong proprietary product margins, and a disciplined capital allocation strategy including increased share repurchases.

Insight Enterprises reported Q3 FY2026 net revenue of $2.4 billion (up 22% YoY) and adjusted diluted EPS of $3.59 (up 34%). Gross profit grew 20%, driven by strong infrastructure hardware growth (>50%) and cloud services, while management raised its full-year 2026 gross profit growth guidance to 12.5%-14% and adjusted EPS midpoint to $13.75.

NerdWallet reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $240 million (up 11% YoY) and non-GAAP operating income of $30 million, both missing the company's guidance range due to a $17 million decline in auto insurance revenue. Management lowered full-year expectations for NGOI to $85-$91 million, citing continued negative impact from vertical integration investments and AI projects. While consumer revenue grew 12% YoY, organic search traffic has stabilized after severe declines, and the company expects Q4 revenue of $191-$203 million.

PENN reported record Q3 FY2026 retail revenue of $1.5 billion and Adjusted EBITDA of $502 million, representing a 5% YoY increase in revenue and 7.7% in Adjusted EBITDA. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for retail revenue to $5.89 billion and Adjusted EBITDA to $1.973 billion, citing strong performance from new development projects like M Resort and Hollywood Columbus. Interactive segment revenue was $348.4 million with a loss of $18.3 million, though margins expanded significantly due to iCasino mix improvements.

The company delivered combined revenue of CAD 438 million, up CAD 47 million year-over-year driven by an acquired entity in Australia and organic growth in Canada, though gross margins were pressured by a significant project loss on the Fargo joint venture. Management lowered full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to a midpoint of CAD 385 million from CAD 400 million due to operational challenges in Australia and the Fargo impact, while raising revenue guidance slightly to a midpoint of CAD 1.75 billion. The CFO noted that Australian margins are expected to normalize to the 15%-20% range in 2027 following Q4 recovery.

National MI reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $187.5 million and adjusted net income of $93.7 million ($1.23 EPS), beating the prior quarter's results despite a sequential decline in NIW volume to $13.6 billion from $14.0 billion implied by the YoY comparison. The company ended with a record $229.7 billion of primary insurance-in-force and maintained strong credit performance with a 1.23% default rate, though persistency dipped slightly to 80.8%. Management expressed confidence in the business outlook while noting that macro risks remain and that Q4 expenses may be seasonally higher.

Omada Health reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $91 million, a 34% year-over-year increase and its highest quarterly revenue ever, driven by strong enrollments and a mix shift toward higher-value diabetes and hypertension programs. Gross margin expanded significantly to 78% on a non-GAAP basis (up from 68% a year ago) as the company achieved record net income of nearly $7 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $12 million. Management raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $344-$346 million and Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $32-$34 million, citing strong execution and operating leverage.

Third quarter sales were $305 million, down approximately 8% on a reported basis primarily due to the divestiture of the Road Markings product line, while excluding that segment sales increased 2%. Adjusted EBITDA was $108 million (down 2%), with margins expanding 230 bps to 35.4%, and diluted adjusted EPS rose 24% to $1.63. Management maintained the full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook at a midpoint of $390 million despite higher input costs and softer demand in Pavement Technologies.

Cloudflare reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $782.5 million, a 39% year-over-year increase, with operating income rising to $137.1 million (17.5% margin). Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $2.963 billion-$2.964 billion (up from prior expectations) and Q4 guidance to $845 million-$846 million, citing accelerating demand in the Workers Developer Platform and agentic workloads. The company added over 158,000 paying customers and crossed $3 billion in annualized revenue.

NACCO reported Q3 FY2026 operating profit of $9.3 million (up 37% YoY) and consolidated adjusted EBITDA of $20.4 million (up 63% YoY), driven by strong utility coal mining and contract mining performance despite $3.4 million in solar curtailment costs. Management expects full-year 2026 operating profit to be comparable to 2025 due to anticipated Q4 softness, while projecting meaningful year-over-year improvements in earnings and cash flow for 2027 as new contracts mature. The company maintains its dividend since 1961 and continues to prioritize selective growth investments over share buybacks at this stage.

N-able reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $137 million (approx. 5% YoY growth) and Adjusted EBITDA of $43.6 million (32% margin). Total ARR grew 5% YoY to $553 million, with gross retention holding steady at mid-80s levels. Management maintained full-year 2026 guidance for revenue between $541-$542 million and Adjusted EBITDA margins of approximately 29%, noting FX headwinds but expressing confidence in new product SKUs like DRaaS and Google Workspace Backup.

Q2 FY2027 revenue rose ~5% to $889 million with Adjusted EBITDA of $287 million and a 32.2% margin, down from the record 34.1% first-half margin. Management cut full-year revenue guidance by 3% at the midpoint to $3.35 billion (Adjusted EBITDA down 1% to $1.015 billion), citing lower resin inflation rather than end-market deterioration, though residential demand also softened with rates near 7.5%. Pre-watch pulled into Q1 was revised up to $40-50 million from $25-30 million, and management pointed to a low-single-digit organic second half with pricing a dollar-for-dollar offset to materials and transport costs.

Murphy Oil beat the top end of its production guidance for Q3 FY2026, driven by the online start of Chinook 8 in the Gulf of America and first oil at Lac Da Vang in Vietnam. Management highlighted that these new assets are expected to generate approximately $1 billion of combined free cash flow over the next five years at $80 Brent. While base business production exceeded expectations, guidance for Q4 was noted as not being strong due to weather impacts and workovers.

MGIC reported Q3 FY2026 net income of $175 million and diluted EPS of $0.85, beating the prior year's $0.83 despite a slight decline in insurance in force growth to 3.6% YoY. Management maintained its initial claim rate assumption at 7.5% while acknowledging that ultimate loss rates are trending upward from historic lows, leading to a cautious outlook on future yields. The company reiterated a commitment to capital returns via dividends and share repurchases, though buyback pace remains price-sensitive.

Perma-Fix reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $17.9 million and a net loss of $3.5 million, representing a decline in profitability compared to the prior year quarter due to lower gross profit in the treatment segment. Management noted that while backlog grew 25% to $19.6 million and pricing increases began implementation, full operations were delayed until September by customer-directed protocol changes and scheduled maintenance. The company expects revenue recognition from the Hanford DFLAW waste stream to continue ramping up over the next few months.

Nova reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $287.8 million (up 28% YoY) and GAAP EPS of $2.64, exceeding the top end of guidance. The company raised its H2 2026 growth guidance to >33% and provided Q4 revenue guidance of $305-$315 million with non-GAAP EPS of $3.03-$3.18. Management highlighted record profitability, strong memory segment performance, and successful acceptance of the AncoScene platform.

Third quarter EBITDA was $2 billion, up 34% year-on-year, driven by structural margin improvements and the new European trade framework (TRQ). Management expects shipment growth to accelerate in Q4 with double-digit year-on-year improvement as destocking normalizes. The full benefits of the TRQ and capacity restarts are expected to materialize fully in 2027.

Oscar Health reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $5.1 billion (up ~70% YoY) and earnings from operations of $178 million, driven by a 24% larger member footprint and favorable risk adjustment. Management raised full-year 2026 earnings from operations guidance to $850-$950 million, citing disciplined execution and AI-driven efficiencies that pushed the SG&A expense ratio down to a record low of 14%. The company expects stable membership in 2027 despite CMS integrity reviews, with pricing increases of ~14% reflecting medical cost trends and market morbidity.

BeOne Medicines reported Q3 FY2026 product revenue of $1.9 billion, a 33% year-over-year increase driven by BRUKINSA sales of $1.4 billion (up 34%) and TEVIMBRA growth of 28%. The company raised its full-year 2026 total revenue guidance to $6.9-$7.0 billion from the prior range of $6.6-$6.8 billion, while narrowing operating expense guidance to $4.9-$5.0 billion. Management highlighted strong commercial execution, broad-based geographic growth, and significant late-stage pipeline progress in both hematology and solid tumors.

Orion reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $67 million (up 16% YoY) and generated $46 million in free cash flow, aided by a one-time timing benefit of approximately $17 million from EU emission allowances. Management raised the midpoint of full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance while reaffirming free cash flow targets, noting that year-to-date results are not materially affected by the allowance timing. The company expects Q4 to be subdued due to seasonality and planned turnaround costs, but remains focused on deleveraging with net leverage at 4.1x.

Onity Group reported Q3 FY2026 results with improved financial performance driven by rising interest rates boosting servicing income, which offset declining origination income. Adjusted pre-tax income more than doubled to $30 million and adjusted ROE reached 19%, while net income available to common stockholders improved to $3.5 million. Management maintained full-year guidance unchanged from the prior quarter, citing a balanced business model that navigates market volatility effectively.

Third quarter revenue was $203 million, a decrease of $22 million year-over-year primarily due to the normalization of recovery services following a significant environmental event in 2025. Adjusted EBITDA was $36 million with a record margin of 17.7%, and full-year 2026 guidance remains unchanged at the midpoint implying approximately 150 basis points of margin expansion compared to 2025.

Blue Owl Capital reported adjusted net investment income of $0.33 per share in Q3 FY2026, exceeding the base dividend of $0.31 and resulting in an annualized ROE of 9.2%. Net asset value increased modestly to $14.32 per share driven by improved portfolio marks and $35 million in share repurchases. Management highlighted that wider spreads on new investments and higher base rates are providing tailwinds, though deal flow remains below historical levels.

Third quarter revenue was $1 billion, up 12% year-over-year, while Contribution Profit rose 70% to $34 million despite a weaker housing market. Contribution Margin declined sequentially to 3.3% from Q2's 5.8% due to watching spring acquisitions into a difficult market and deeper price cuts for clearance. Management expects margins to decline again in Q4 as the company continues clearing inventory and increases marketing spend.

Nyxoah reported Q3 FY2026 global net revenue of EUR 9.2 million (up 19% sequentially and 365% YoY), with U.S. revenue reaching EUR 6.7 million. Gross margin expanded to 63.1%, but the company adjusted its full-year 2026 revenue guidance down to a range of EUR 33-35 million, citing a need for revenues to be more reflective of historical ramps for the new technology. Management emphasized financial discipline and reduced cash burn while maintaining confidence in the Genio product's differentiation.

rows.gics_industry: Independent Power and Renewable Electricity Producers
rows.key_quote: Ormat reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $275 million (up 10.2% YoY) and Adjusted EBITDA of $153.8 million (up 11.1%), driven by a 145% surge in energy storage revenue to $49.9 million. Management raised the full-year revenue guidance midpoint to $1.17-$1.20 billion and Adjusted EBITDA to $640-$650 million, citing strong momentum in storage and electricity segments despite a temporary Puna outage impact.

Nexstar reported record Q3 net revenue of $2.13 billion and record Adjusted EBITDA of $756 million, driven by the TEGNA acquisition and a record-breaking political advertising cycle totaling $1.1 billion for the year. Non-political advertising declined low single digits excluding political crowd-out, while distribution revenue grew 4.2% on a legacy basis. Management reiterated that legacy Nexstar's net distribution guidance remains intact despite the election cycle ending.

Net product revenue declined 70% year-over-year to $45.5 million in Q3 FY2026, driven by a contraction in the skin substitute market following CMS policy changes and discarded product comments. Operating loss widened to $29.5 million compared to income last year due to lower revenue and reduced gross margins (52% vs 76%), though operating expenses decreased significantly by $55.2 million year-over-year. Management updated full-year 2026 guidance to a net revenue range of $179-$200 million, representing a decline of 65%-68%, which is slightly wider than the prior guidance of 62%-68%.

OTF reported Q3 FY2026 net investment income of $0.29 per share, a modest decline from the prior quarter's $0.30 due to lighter deployments and a new non-accrual, while NAV increased to $16.62 driven by portfolio valuation recovery and $55 million in share repurchases. Management maintained its guidance to cover the dividend by mid-next year via approximately $1.2 billion of net deployment and leverage increasing toward 1.15x, citing improved market sentiment and wider spreads as tailwinds. The company raised $900 million in debt financing during the quarter, ending with significant liquidity and a conservative portfolio structure.

Enviri reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted earnings growth of over 20% with total revenue of $325 million and adjusted EBITDA of $47 million, exceeding expectations despite market headwinds. Management raised full-year EBITDA guidance for both Harsco Environmental ($180M-$184M) and Rail (loss range narrowed to $7M-$10M), citing efficiency actions and improved business mix. The company successfully exited the DB contract with a $73 million payment and continues constructive discussions regarding Network Rail.

Third quarter revenue surged 98% year-over-year to $509 million, driven by the inclusion of acquired entities Kirkland's, SFV Services, and The Container Store. Adjusted EBITDA remained at a loss of $26 million, representing a $21 million decline from the prior year quarter due to high integration costs and inventory adjustments. Management provided a sequential revenue guidepost of approximately 5% growth for Q4 but explicitly stated they do not have audited historical data for the acquired businesses.

Microchip reported September-quarter net sales of $1.622 billion, up 9.2% sequentially and 42.2% year-over-year, with non-GAAP gross margin of 66.5% and non-GAAP EPS of $0.97, $0.04 above the midpoint of guidance. However, roughly $53 million of the quarter was one-time (patent licensing, a distribution pricing effect, and a customer contract), so the underlying product growth was more modest. December-quarter guidance calls for revenue of down 3% to up 1% (midpoint -1%), non-GAAP gross margin of 64%-65%, and non-GAAP EPS of $0.87-$0.95, a step down sequentially, which management frames as roughly 5%-7% above normal seasonality after stripping the one-offs. Bookings were strong and book-to-bill remained above one, backlog built, and management cited supply constraints and stretched lead times of six to 32 weeks limiting shipments of high-margin products.

Consolidated revenues grew 9% YoY to $145M OIBDA (up 6%) and $103M AFFO (up 5%), driven by strong 20% growth in transit and mid-single-digit growth in billboard. Management raised full-year AFFO guidance to approximately 25% growth compared to the prior year, citing robust Q4 bookings and continued investment in AI-enabled sales tools. The quarter included roughly $50M of incremental FIFA World Cup revenue, with management expressing high confidence in sustaining momentum into 2027.

Q3 revenue grew 14% YoY to $78.8 million and Adjusted EBITDA was $10.3 million (13% margin), finishing above the high end of guidance. Platform WAU reached a record 24.5 million, up 7% sequentially and 14% YoY, driven by organic reactivation without paid user acquisition. Management raised Q4 revenue guidance to $78-$80 million and Adjusted EBITDA to $10-$11 million, citing strong advertiser demand and new product rollouts.

Northwest Natural Holding Company reported Q3 FY2026 results with a loss of $0.71 per share, an improvement from the $0.73 loss in the prior year quarter, driven by higher margins and cost discipline. Management raised full-year 2026 EPS guidance to $3.10-$3.20, citing strong year-to-date performance and constructive regulatory outcomes including a SiEnergy settlement and new rates in Oregon and Washington. The company also announced its largest dividend increase since 2012, raising the annual dividend to $2 per share.

Pan American Silver reported Q3 FY2026 attributable free cash flow of $377 million and net earnings of $357 million ($0.86/share), though silver production of 6.1M ounces missed the quarterly outlook range due to sequencing at Juanicipio and Cerro Moro, and gold production was impacted by delays at Timmins and Shahuindo. Management revised full-year gold production guidance downward to 660k-680k ounces and raised full-year gold all-in sustaining cost guidance to $2,000-$2,150/oz due to lower production, increased development costs, and El Niño weather impacts. While silver segment costs came in below expectations at $11.21/oz, the company faces operational headwinds including a 40-day downtime at Huaron for mill repairs and ongoing remediation work at Jacobina affecting 2027 production.

PAR reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $137.1 million (up 15% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $17.1 million, exceeding the high end of guidance. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $532.5-$536.5 million from the prior $516-$523 million range, citing strong ARR growth and multi-product adoption. The company delivered record free cash flow of $17.7 million and improved non-GAAP subscription margins sequentially.

Puma reported Q3 FY2026 net product revenue of $54.1 million, a sequential increase driven by inventory drawdowns and higher supply revenue to international partners, though underlying U.S. net sales declined quarter-over-quarter. Management lowered full-year 2026 guidance for both net NERLYNX product revenue ($205M-$208M vs prior $205M-$209M) and royalties ($18M-$19M vs prior $20M-$23M) due to generic competition in China and higher Medicaid gross-to-net adjustments. The company remains debt-free with positive net income guidance for the full year.

NorthWestern Energy reported Q3 FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS of $0.50 versus $0.62 in the prior year quarter, while non-GAAP diluted EPS was $0.58 compared to $0.79 last year. Management reaffirmed its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance range of $3.68-$3.83 with a bias toward the lower half due to weak market prices and weather impacts offsetting margin improvements. The company declared a quarterly dividend of $0.67 per share and anticipates completing the merger with Black Hills Corporation by year-end pending final Montana PSC approval.

PDF Solutions reported record Q3 revenue of $68.3 million, representing a 20% year-over-year increase and an 11% quarter-over-quarter rise. The company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 guidance for 20% annual revenue growth and maintained its long-term target gross margin model of 77%. Gross margins expanded to 77% from 73% in the prior quarter, driven by reduced eProbe costs and controlled personnel spending.

Revenue rose 3% to $1.2 billion with DAT up 20% and Communication Services down 3%; net loss widened $68 million to $129 million and adjusted EBITDA fell 4% to $370 million. Full-year EBITDA guidance was cut to roughly flat versus prior year, while free cash flow guidance improved to over $225 million and CapEx was trimmed to $850-900 million. Management disclosed that recent airline announcements will ultimately affect 15%-20% of aviation revenue and guided FY2028 aviation revenue below FY2027, offsetting an awards pipeline that includes about $2 billion of DAT awards planned for FY2027 versus $1.6 billion last year.

NHP reported Q3 FY2026 same-store cash NOI growth of 13.6% and a same-store cash NOI margin expansion of 150 bps to 24.3%, driven by higher occupancy and pricing power following the deployment of short-term concessions. Management raised its full-year 2026 SHOP same-store cash NOI growth guidance to 16.5%-18.5% and confirmed the completion of a significant OMF portfolio exit with $1.1 billion in gross proceeds. The company is transitioning to a pure-play senior housing REIT with a strengthened balance sheet, having retired preferred equity and reduced secured debt.

OceanaGold reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $655 million and adjusted EPS of $0.94, representing a significant beat against consensus estimates. The company generated $155 million in free cash flow and returned $79 million to shareholders via buybacks and dividends, ending the quarter with $729 million in cash and zero debt. Management confirmed they remain on track to meet full-year production guidance, expecting Q4 to be the strongest quarter of the year driven by higher production at Haile and Didipio.

Q2 FY2027 revenue rose 9% YoY to $21.7 million from $19.9 million, with LED lighting up to $14.9 million from $10.7 million, offset by EV charging falling to $2.8 million from $4.8 million and maintenance to $4.0 million from $4.5 million. Overall gross margin contracted to 28.7% from 31.0% on mix shift within lighting, opex rose to $7.0 million from $6.4 million, and the net loss widened to $0.8 million ($0.20 per share) from $0.6 million ($0.17). Management reaffirmed full-year revenue guidance of $100-$102 million (recently raised from $95-$97 million) with positive adjusted EBITDA, and guided Q3 and Q4 to roughly even revenue near $26-27 million each with gross margin normalizing back above 30%. Backlog was $21.6-21.7 million at September 30, with firm POs for the $10-15 million retailer interior project received after quarter-end, implying a substantially higher October backlog that management declined to quantify.

Q2 constant-currency revenue rose 10%, above the prior mid-single-digit outlook, with Asia +28% (China +35%), North America +6%, and Europe +3%. Adjusted gross margin expanded 220 bps to 70.2% and operating margin 140 bps to 15.5%, with AUR +9%. FY2027 guidance was raised: revenue growth to ~6%-7% from 5%-6%, gross margin expansion to ~80-100 bps from 50-70 bps, and operating margin expansion to ~80-100 bps from 60-80 bps. Europe's outlook was trimmed to low single digits from low-to-mid single digits on weaker traffic and consumer confidence, and the company repurchased ~$250 million in shares in the quarter, completing FY2027 buyback plans.

MP Materials reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $155.8 million (including PPA income), a 23.6% sequential increase driven by NdPr sales volumes up 94% year-over-year and higher realized prices. Adjusted EBITDA rose significantly to $53.7 million year-over-year, supported by the commercial launch of dysprosium and terbium separation circuits and the qualification of magnets for GM. Management raised full-year capital expenditure guidance to $500-$600 million due to heavy rare earth expansion and Chlor-Alkali startup, while maintaining strong liquidity of $1.34 billion.

UHAL reported Q2 FY2027 earnings of $137 million ($0.71 per non-voting share) versus $106 million ($0.54) a year ago, on record total revenue with equipment rental revenue up $37 million and storage revenue up $16 million (~6%). Moving and storage Adjusted EBITDA rose $5 million to $548 million, but the Adjusted EBITDA margin fell about 90 bps as freight and shipping costs added just under $24.5 million. Same-store occupancy declined 110 bps to 89.5%, and management disclosed no formal forward guidance other than reiterating a projected ~$500 million net fleet CapEx reduction and describing the dealer-expansion catalyst as progressing slower than hoped.

STERIS reported Q2 FY27 revenue of $1.6 billion, up 9% as-reported and 8% constant currency organic, with adjusted EPS of $2.94 (+19%, +13% excluding tariff refunds) versus $2.47 last year. Adjusted gross margin rose 100 bps to 45.3% and adjusted EBIT margin 150 bps to 24.6%, both largely driven by ~$20 million of tariff refunds; underlying margins were down slightly as price was offset by inflation. FY27 EPS guidance was raised to $11.35-$11.55 from $11.10-$11.30 (including ~$0.18 of tariff refund benefit), while total revenue growth guidance was unchanged at 7-8% as-reported / 6-7% organic; AST was trimmed to 6-7% from 7-8% and Life Sciences raised to 9-10% from 6-7%. Free cash flow for the first half fell to $492.5 million from $527.7 million on lower working capital contribution, and a new restructuring plan with $45 million of charges and ~$9 million of annualized savings was approved.

Universal reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $622 million, down 18% YoY, operating income of $43 million versus $68 million, and net income of $13 million versus $34 million. Tobacco segment revenue fell 19% to $534 million and operating income fell to $44 million from $65 million on delayed shipment timing; Ingredients revenue fell 8% to $88 million and swung to a $2 million operating loss. Management maintained that full-year expectations are unchanged, with shipments and results heavily weighted to the second half, and reported uncommitted flue-cured and burley stocks down 45 million kilos to 134 million kilos (19% of inventory, within target range). Net debt rose $82 million YoY to $1.15 billion, with management citing plans to delever as working capital moderates.

Sony reported record Q2 FY2026 results with sales up 10% YoY to JPY 3,429.4 billion and operating income up 45% to JPY 622.3 billion, with net income up 44% to JPY 449.6 billion. Full-year guidance was raised across all three metrics: sales +4% to JPY 13 trillion, operating income +9% to JPY 1,870 billion, and net income +10% to JPY 1,330 billion. Segment guidance was lifted for G&NS (OI +6% to JPY 700 billion), Music (+6% to JPY 445 billion), Pictures (+33% to JPY 200 billion), and I&SS (+7% to JPY 450 billion), while ET&S was unchanged. Offsets include a JPY 16 billion earthquake loss at Kumamoto, a JPY 30 billion Sony Honda Mobility loss, a ~20% YoY smartphone market decline, and a delayed God of War Laufey release.

Marex reported a record Q3 FY2026 with revenue surging 53% year-over-year to $743 million and adjusted profit before tax rising 75% to $176 million. Management highlighted structural growth from acquisitions like Levmet and Webb Traders, which are already performing above pre-acquisition run rates, alongside strong organic expansion in FX and Prime businesses. The company reiterated its strategy of diversifying earnings streams to deliver sustainable growth across market environments.

ePlus reported Q2 FY2027 net sales of $667.9M, up 9.7% YoY, with product sales up 12.8% to $547.1M and record gross billings of $1.07B. Gross profit rose 11.2% to $180.3M, gross margin expanded 40 bps to 27%, operating income grew 15.8% to $56.5M, and non-GAAP EPS rose 19% to $1.82. Management raised FY2027 guidance to upper single-digit growth in net sales and gross profit, with adjusted EBITDA up low double digits. Open orders rose nearly $750M YoY to about $1.8B, driven by AI, data center, and cloud demand, while professional services revenue declined 11.3% on retail project delays.

Third quarter revenue was $212.2 million, up 18.8% year-over-year, with diluted EPS of $0.53 compared to $0.27 in the prior year. Management maintained full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $850 million-$900 million and expects gross margins to be approximately 14%, slightly higher than previously anticipated due to a decrease in chassis sales. The company returned $5.1 million to shareholders via dividends and share repurchases.

Q2 FY2027 revenue of $336.3M grew 22.7% YoY but fell 1.6% organically, with the growth entirely driven by the first full quarter of Breathe Right and LaCorium; adjusted EPS rose ~6% to $1.13 and adjusted EBITDA margin was ~33.6%. Management lowered the FY2027 outlook to $1.28-1.29B revenue and $4.48-4.55 adjusted EPS, citing Clear Eyes production volatility that began in late September and continued into October with zero safety stock, plus slightly higher interest expense. Full-year Clear Eyes sales are now forecast below $20M with limited second-half improvement, while the ~$190M Breathe Right/LaCorium contribution and ~2% organic growth excluding Clear Eyes are unchanged. Adjusted free cash flow is now expected at least $265M, down slightly on updated revenue and interest assumptions.

MKS reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.41 billion, beating the high end of guidance with 43% year-over-year growth and expanding operating margins by approximately 700 basis points to 27.8%. The company raised its full-year outlook, projecting nearly 40% annual growth for the E&P business driven by AI demand, and provided a Q4 revenue guidance of $1.49 billion plus or minus $40 million. Management highlighted strong order flow extending into 2028 and announced a new $500 million share repurchase program alongside a dividend payment.

Mobia Medical reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $15.6 million, a 73% year-over-year increase driven by the expansion of active territories to 40 and strong adoption in existing programs. Gross margin expanded to 83.2% due to lower freight and tariff costs. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $57.0-$57.5 million from a prior range of $54.0-$56.0 million.

Q2 FY2027 revenue rose 1.4% to $222.2M as expected, with product revenue down 5.1% to $89.9M on order timing pulled into Q1 while service revenue grew 6.4% to $132.3M. Non-GAAP EPS was $0.71 versus $0.62, operating margin expanded to 28.3% from 26.5% on 2.7% lower opex, and gross margin slipped to 80.9% from 81.4% on DDoS acquisition overhead. Management reaffirmed full-year revenue of $885-915M and EPS of $2.65-2.80, guiding Q3 revenue to $240-250M and EPS to $0.90-0.95 against a tough comparison with $15M pulled forward last year. Free cash flow was a $17.8M use tied to working capital, and the company repurchased about 2M shares for roughly $77M.

Total Q2 revenue fell 5.5% YoY to $632M, described as favorable to expectations despite lower math capture rates, while Higher Ed was up slightly and K-12 fell 9.6% to $325M. Adjusted EBITDA was $251M at a 39.6% margin and gross margin held at 79.2%; first-half revenue was $1.2B, down 1.9%. FY2027 guidance was reaffirmed at $2.115B-2.175B revenue and $750M-790M adjusted EBITDA (~35.9% margin, up 50 bps), with the only change being a softer enrollment assumption of flat to down 1% versus 1% growth prior. Management pointed to FY2028 acceleration from the K-12 ELA super cycle, MCP/AI integrations, and a two-business-unit leadership change.

Third quarter revenue reached a record $652.6 million, beating the high end of guidance, while adjusted EBITDA of $156 million and EPS of $2.07 also finished above the high end of guidance. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for revenue to $2.519-$2.534 billion, adjusted EBITDA to $589-$593 million, and adjusted EPS to $7.13-$7.29. The company announced a CEO succession with Steve Spittle taking over on April 1, 2027, following the separation of its food processing business.

Third quarter revenue was $101.9 million, up 24% year-over-year, driven by a doubling of commercial product revenue to $45 million led by FUROSCIX ReadyFlow. GAAP net loss widened to $23.2 million due to $11.6 million in CVR expenses and $5.2 million in amortization related to the scPharma acquisition. Management expects to return to profitability in Q4 2026 on both GAAP and non-GAAP bases, with full-year 2027 profitability anticipated.

Consolidated adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations rose 15% YoY to $192.4 million, with Water Solutions adjusted EBITDA up 17% to $178.3 million (93% of the total) on record produced water disposal of 3.45 million barrels per day, up 23% YoY. Management raised FY2027 adjusted EBITDA guidance by $10 million to $735-$745 million (second raise this fiscal year) and lifted FY2027 growth capex to roughly $250-$270 million from about $200 million. Water Solutions opex fell to $0.20 per barrel from $0.22, while Crude Oil Logistics adjusted EBITDA declined to $11.9 million from $16.6 million on Grand Mesa volumes of 64,000 bpd versus 72,000 bpd. Leverage is expected to reach about four times by fiscal year-end, with the credit agreement repriced 50 bps lower and the ABL accordion raised $50 million to $475 million.

Magnolia Oil & Gas reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted net income of $166 million ($0.71 per share) and adjusted EBITDAX of $392 million, with production volumes growing 17% year-over-year to 117.3k BOE/d despite a partial WildFire acquisition period. Drilling and completion capital was $147 million, running below earlier guidance due to the short integration window, while adjusted free cash flow reached $224 million. Management provided unchanged Q4 guidance for production of 159k-161k BOE/d and a D&C budget of approximately $235 million.

Monster Beverage reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $2.56 billion, a 16.7% increase year-over-year driven by strong international growth (28.1%) and solid U.S. performance (9.5%). Gross margin decreased to 54.7% due to higher aluminum costs and geographic mix shifts, while operating income rose 6.4% to $718.7 million. Management highlighted robust category health globally but declined to provide specific forward guidance or raise expectations.

StepStone reported fee revenues of $298 million (up 37% YoY) and FRE of $126 million (up 61% YoY), with a 42% core FRE margin, up 6 pts YoY, and adjusted net income of $0.66 per share versus $0.54 a year ago. Gross AUM additions were $11 billion in the quarter and a record $43 billion over 12 months, with fee-earning AUM at $158 billion and undeployed fee-earning capital at $42 billion. Management guided to a roughly 42% full-year cash compensation ratio (better than the prior 43% signal) and meaningful margin improvement versus last year, while cautioning that 42% is not a run rate and that G&A will be seasonally higher in fiscal Q3 and Q4. The company plans to retain cash to fund the private wealth profits interest watch-in, suspending the supplemental dividend while maintaining the $0.33 regular quarterly dividend, and a GAAP net loss of $71 million ($0.87 per share) reflected the change in fair value of that watch-in.

Microchip reported September-quarter net sales of $1.622 billion, up 9.2% sequentially and 42.2% year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.97 beating the guidance midpoint by $0.04; non-GAAP gross margin was 66.5% and operating margin 39.5%. About $53 million of infrequent, 100%-margin items (patent licensing, distribution price-protection catch-up, a $10 million customer contract) boosted the quarter and do not repeat. December-quarter guidance is down 3% to up 1% sequentially (midpoint -1%), with non-GAAP gross margin of 64%-65% and EPS of $0.87-$0.95; management frames this as 5%-7% above normal seasonality but below what it expected a quarter ago. Management cited supply constraints at foundries, OSATs and internal fabs, with lead times stretching to six to 32 weeks and unsupported high-margin backlog pushed to later quarters; bookings were strong and book-to-bill well above one.

Q3 FY2026 revenue fell 1.1% to $506.5M as attendance dropped 4.7% (~320,000 guests) on weather, calendar and international headwinds, partly offset by total revenue per capita up 3.8%. Adjusted EBITDA declined $11.2M to $205.1M and net income fell to $80.0M from $89.3M; nine-month revenue was down 1.6% and Adjusted EBITDA down $31.4M. Management gave no formal 2026 or 2027 guidance, declining to commit to Q4 EBITDA growth given continued weather disruption, but cited a positive paid pass base (+0.3% through October), 2027-specific pass products up over 15%, deferred revenue up 4.9%, and a new $40M-$50M 2027 gross cost-savings target on top of the $50M 2026 program. The company bought back ~$218M of stock (~12% of shares) year-to-date but made no Q3 purchases due to cash flow timing.

Nuvation Bio reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $45 million, driven by $27.5 million in U.S. net IBTROZI product revenue (18% sequential growth) and $17.5 million in collaboration/license revenue. Despite a 15% decline in total new patient starts across the ROS1 TKI market, the company maintained its position as the leading ROS1 TKI with over 60% share of first-line new patient starts. Management reiterated that quarterly fluctuations are expected in this ultra-rare disease and provided no specific financial guidance updates.

Progyny reported record revenue and profitability for Q3 FY2026, driven by a strong watching season that added 1.3 million new covered lives and over 85 new clients. Management raised the midpoint of full-year 2026 guidance to $1.365 billion-$1.385 billion (5.9%-7.5% growth) and expects Q4 revenue between $344.7 million and $364.7 million. Gross margin expanded 130 bps year-over-year due to reduced stock compensation and operational efficiencies, while the company generated over $56 million in operating cash flow.

Q3 net sales were ~$1.05B, up 8% YoY and above the top end of guidance, with GAAP diluted EPS of $0.50 and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.80. Adjusted EBITDA rose 13% to $265M and margin expanded 109 bps to 25.3%, led by Electronic & Specialty Materials sales up 13% (electronic materials +31%) and refrigerants +8%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for a second consecutive quarter to net sales of $4.195-$4.22B and adjusted EBITDA of $1.05-$1.06B, while Q4 guidance implies sequential moderation. Nuclear sales grew only 4% on ~$30M of product loan returns, and Building Solutions & Intermediates declined 5% on construction softness.

For the third quarter of 2026, revenue was $5.2 million, an increase from $3.7 million in the prior year period driven by license revenue. R&D expenses rose to $35.5 million and SG&A increased to $23.9 million due to recruitment and launch preparation costs. The FDA accepted the BLA for AMT-130 with a PDUFA date of May 1, 2027, and the MHRA validated the MAA in the UK.

Smith & Nephew reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.55 billion, up 3.4% underlying and 3.4% reported with no FX impact, an acceleration from Q2, but cut full-year guidance to approximately 3% revenue growth (trading profit to about $1.25 billion, FCF about $750 million) citing no expected material improvement in U.S. knees and hips. Sports Medicine & ENT grew 7.9% with joint repair up 11.2%, wound declined 0.2% on an 8.8% bioactives fall, and orthopedics returned to growth at 2.5% while U.S. knees and hips stayed weak. Management disclosed that discussions with J&J over DePuy Synthes had ended, while a broader strategic review of orthopedics remains active. The guidance cut follows prior reductions and comes before the LANDMARK cemented launch in Q2 2027 and CORI Hip in Q1 2027.

Qnity reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $1.6 billion, representing a 22% year-over-year increase and 9% sequential growth. Adjusted EPS rose 55% year-over-year to $1.46, while adjusted gross margin expanded 270 bps to 47.8%. Management raised full-year revenue guidance by $200 million and adjusted EPS by $0.50 at the midpoint.

Nuvectis Pharma reported a net loss of $30.1 million for Q3 FY2026, excluding upfront license payments and milestones, with an adjusted net loss of $5.8 million. The company ended the quarter with approximately $140 million in cash, providing a runway into the second half of 2029. Management highlighted significant pipeline progress, including China approval for NXP100 (ciprocopan) in PNH and breakthrough designation for NXP200 in glioma, while outlining plans to file US INDs by year-end.

Snap reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.72 billion, up 14% year-over-year and within the prior guidance range of $1.70-$1.74 billion, with gross margin of 62% (up ~7 points), net income of $56 million, and adjusted EBITDA of $383 million (22% margin). Advertising revenue grew just 4% as upper-funnel brand advertising declined, while other revenue grew 84% and paid subscribers surpassed 30 million. Q4 revenue guidance is $1.950-$1.985 billion with adjusted EBITDA of $490-$525 million, and full-year infrastructure cost guidance was narrowed to $1.65-$1.66 billion from $1.65-$1.70 billion. Management also announced a shift to global MAU and MAU-based ARPU as primary metrics beginning Q1 2027.

Ralliant reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $620 million, a 17% increase year-over-year, with adjusted EPS of $0.93 representing a 64% normalized growth. The company delivered on all metrics above the high end of its guidance ranges and raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $2.34 billion-$2.36 billion, an increase of $75 million at the midpoint compared to prior expectations. Management highlighted broad-based demand acceleration across defense, utilities, and industrial markets, supported by a backlog exceeding $1.5 billion in defense and strong organic growth in Test and Measurement.

NETGEAR reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $167.3 million, down 9.3% year-over-year and below the midpoint of its guidance range ($165M-$175M), primarily due to manufacturing constraints at a key partner that limited supply fulfillment despite robust underlying demand. The company delivered non-GAAP EPS of $0.13 and non-GAAP operating income above the high end of its guidance range, reflecting strong enterprise margins (53.2%) but offset by a consumer contribution loss of $1.4 million. Management raised Q4 revenue guidance to $160M-$175M, acknowledging that production delays will persist into Q1 2027.

Pattern reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $886 million, up 38% year-over-year (approx. 42% adjusted for timing shifts), and Adjusted EBITDA of $57 million, a 40% increase. Management raised its full-year revenue outlook to approximately $3.5 billion and Adjusted EBITDA to roughly $220 million, citing strong Net Revenue Retention (NRR) of 127% and record new brand partnerships. The company highlighted significant growth in non-Amazon revenue (+86%) and international revenue (+56%), while maintaining a net cash position with no debt.

PSBD reported Q3 FY2026 net investment income of $11.6 million ($0.38 per share), missing the prior year's $13.6 million due to lower base rates and portfolio paydowns, while NAV per share declined slightly from $13.21 to $13.34 after a volatile quarter with rate hikes in September. Management maintained a cautious outlook on deal activity citing elevated interest rate volatility and geopolitical uncertainty, though they affirmed confidence in the sustainability of the base dividend and prioritized share repurchases.

Q3 FY2026 net sales were $83.4M, down 12% YoY, but up 21% excluding the prior-year $25.9M China deferred sales; China grew 31% ex-deferred item and ex-China rose 13%. GAAP net income was $5.6M ($0.11/diluted share) versus a $6.3M net loss ($0.13) ex-item a year ago, with adjusted EBITDA of $14.4M ($0.28/share) versus $8.9M ($0.18) ex-item. Gross margin fell to 70.9% from 82.2% (75.5% ex-item), pressured by ERP-related low production volumes, freight, tariffs, and inventory provisions; management expects Q4 gross margin above Q3 and further improvement in 2027. No formal Q4 or FY2027 guidance was given, though management said China would grow versus last year with a seasonal Q4 decline, and the $225M adjusted opex target was reaffirmed; a $50M buyback was authorized in September.

Power Integrations reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $125.5 million, up 6% year-over-year and 5% sequentially, with non-GAAP EPS rising 28% to $0.46. The company beat its gross margin outlook and reduced inventory by over $7 million, though channel stock rose to 11.8 weeks due to soft consumer demand and supply constraints in high-power segments. Management raised the quarterly dividend to $0.22 per share starting Q1 2027 and provided a Q4 revenue guidance range of $118-$126 million.

Talos reported Q3 FY2026 total production of ~92,000 BOE/d (oil ~69,000 bpd), both exceeding guidance, with adjusted EBITDA ~$406M and adjusted free cash flow ~$186M on premium oil realizations ~$1.60/bbl above WTI. The company raised full-year 2026 production guidance to 68,000-70,000 bpd oil and 92.5-94.5 BOE/d (~8% oil increase at midpoint vs. original guidance), funding the $420M Gulf of America bolt-on while keeping leverage at 0.6x and the revolver undrawn. Total capital and P&A spend is unchanged from the original plan, with capex guidance lowered at the midpoint and P&A raised. Daenerys appraisal remains ongoing with a 2027 sidetrack and no development decision yet.

Core net sales declined 1.7% year-over-year to $989 million all-in, while core adjusted operating margin decreased 210 basis points to 14.3%. Management updated the full-year outlook to reflect a more measured retailer inventory position ahead of the cough and cold season and continued softness in Europe, resulting in lower guidance for both core and all-in net sales compared to prior expectations.

Nomad Foods reported Q3 FY2026 results where management held EBITDA guidance despite negative EBITDA expectations for Q4 driven by inflation on fish and pricing variability. The company reiterated its 2027 outlook with gross inflation assumptions around 7% and savings targets of roughly 3%, maintaining a net inflation expectation of 4%. While the CEO expressed satisfaction in maintaining guidance, the forward range for Q4 implies significant downside risk from cost pressures.

PROCEPT BioRobotics reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $98.3 million (18% YoY growth) and completed 13,400 U.S. procedures (22% YoY growth). The company remained on track to meet its full-year 2026 guidance of $390-$410 million revenue and 54,000-56,000 procedures, with Q4 expected to be EBITDA positive. Gross margin expanded to 66% from 65% in the prior year.

Southwest Gas reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS from continuing operations of $0.20 versus $0.06 a year ago, with year-to-date adjusted EPS of $2.69, up 18%, driven by California rate relief, customer growth, and flat O&M. Management reaffirmed 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $4.17-$4.32 (centering around the midpoint) and the 12%-14% long-term EPS growth target; no guidance was raised. Final orders in California (~$32M) and Nevada (~$48M) deliver ~$80M of incremental annual revenue, while Arizona remains pending with staff context $53-58M versus the company's updated $91.3M request. The quarter benefited from roughly $0.12 of non-recurring items (D&A true-up and state tax benefit) that management said were not fully in plan.

Adjusted EPS of $2.31 beat the midpoint of guidance by $0.76, but $0.67 of that came from net IEEPA tariff refunds rather than operations; above-the-line operating performance was 'largely in line' with expectations. Adjusted gross margin of 39.4% included about 430 bps of tariff benefit, with the remaining ~350 bps of YoY improvement driven by productivity and mix.
